papers.abstract_full: Polygenic scores (PGS) predict an individual's genetic value for a complex trait of interest by aggregating effect size estimates from genome-wide association studies (GWAS). While powerful, this approach assumes that genetic variants affect the phenotype in an additive way, which might be problematic when dominance is part of the genetic architecture. To address this limitation, we developed PGS a,d , a simple polygenic scoring framework, rooted in quantitative genetics theory, that incorporates both additive ( a ) and dominance effects ( d ) directly. We evaluated PGS a,d against the standard GWAS-based PGS (PGS β ) in simulations. The results showed that PGS a,d consistently achieved lower root mean squared error (RMSE) and progressively higher R 2 as dominance contributed more to the genetic architecture. We then applied the method to 16 blood cell traits, height, and body mass index (BMI) from UK Biobank. PGS a,d showed comparable R 2 to PGS β for all traits (including height and BMI whose architecture is predominantly additive) and significantly lower RMSE for four traits after strict Bonferroni correction. Across traits, RMSE improvement from PGS a,d was positively associated with the magnitude of the estimated dominance effects, whereby traits with larger dominance effects displayed lower RMSE from PGS a,d . As a byproduct of our analysis, we also identified 141 variants in 39 genomic regions with significant dominance effects after Bonferroni correction across traits, recapitulating known associations and identifying novel ones. Together, these results show that explicitly modeling additive and dominance effects is a robust strategy that can improve individual-level predictions, especially when dominance contributes to complex trait architecture.

papers.abstract_full: Conventional confirmation of Listeria monocytogenes from food samples involves enrichment, selective plating, and biochemical identification. Colony confirmation is a process that can take 3-5 days. We validated a multiplex PCR assay for the rapid identification of Listeria colonies at the genus level and the specific detection of L. monocytogenes directly from both selective and non-selective agars. The assay targets three markers: hlyA (152 bp, L. monocytogenes-specific), prs (370 bp, Listeria genus-specific), and 16S rRNA (107 bp, internal amplification control). Validation using 226 isolates (117 L. monocytogenes, 44 other Listeria spp., 65 non-Listeria) demonstrated 100% inclusivity and 100% exclusivity. Results were consistent across Oxford, Agar Listeria media, RAPID'L.mono, PALCAM, with isolate identifications confirmed by whole-genome sequencing. Although MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry also provides rapid identification, it requires specialized instrumentation and may not be available in all food microbiology laboratories. In contrast, this PCR assay reduces turnaround time to less than 4 hours and aligns with ISO 16140-6 and Health Canada guidelines for confirmatory testing. Additional evaluation of recently described Listeria species and haemolytic L. innocua strains, presented separately, identified atypical amplification profiles that highlight potential imitation in the broader applicability of the assay.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is widely used for screening and diagnosis of prostate cancer (CaP). Variation in PSA levels is influenced by age, genetics and other factors, yet this variation has not been well characterized in African men. METHODS: We used data on serum PSA extracted from medical records from prostate cancer cases and controls collected as part of the Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP) network. We evaluate the association of PSA levels with country of origin, age, body mass index (BMI), and polygenic risk score (PRS). RESULTS: The median PSA levels were 41.8 (0.2-9696) ng/ml in 1,907 prostate cancer cases and 1.235 (0.01-9.72) ng/ml in 902 controls. papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: We report the results of a Phase 1 study of TAVO412, an anti-EGFR, cMET, and VEGF-A multi-specific antibody. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients of age ≥18 years with advanced solid tumors refractory to standard therapies were enrolled (TAVO412-CN001, NCT06761651). The study used a standard 3 + 3 design for dose-escalation from 150 to 1500 mg every two weeks in a 28-day cycle. Patients were backfilled for further assessment of safety and preliminary anti-tumor activities. RESULTS: The study included 67 patients, with 6 tumor types. Serum drug exposures increased with the dose. TAVO412 had low immunogenicity (5.9%). No DLTs were reported and the MTD was not reached up to 1500 mg. The most common treatment-related (TR) AEs (≥30%) across all doses were rash, hypoalbuminemia, stomatitis, infusion related reaction, increased ALT, and hypokalemia. Preliminary anti-tumor activities were observed in NSCLC patients (n = 27) with 5 PRs (3 of 9 EGFR Exon20ins and 2 of 12 Exon21 L858R) and 13 SDs, in ESCC (n = 11) with 1 PR and 8 SDs, and in CRC (n = 15) with 4 PRs and 7 SDs, in the dose range from 750 to 1500 mg. All PRs were confirmed except 1. The longest treatment duration was approximately 39 weeks. Baseline soluble VEGF-A levels correlated with treatment responses. CONCLUSIONS: TAVO412 was tolerated up to 1500 mg, with mostly target-related AEs. Preliminary activities of TAVO412 were observed in CRC, ESCC, and NSCLC patients who had been heavily treated. Further evaluation of TAVO412 in patients with these tumor types is warranted.

papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains without effective treatment, largely due to the fact that clinical symptoms emerge only after decades of silent pathological progression. papers.abstract_full: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains without effective treatment, largely due to the fact that clinical symptoms emerge only after decades of silent pathological progression. It is urgently needed to identify modifiable risk factors in earlier life stages, when preventive interventions may still be effective. Functional connectivity (FC) has emerged as a promising neuromarker for both neurodegenerative processes and behavioral traits, making it a potential bridge between early-life health profiles and late-life AD risk. In this work, we introduce a novel integrative framework, called InterventionVAE, that models how early-life lifestyle and physiological factors influence AD risk through their impact on brain FC. Our approach combines a modified variational autoencoder (VAE) that simulates FC changes under interventions with a predictive model that estimates AD risk based on FC patterns. This design enables training of the generative and predictive components under different datasets and populations, with FC acting as the bridge between early-life modifiable factors and late-life disease risk. Applying InterventionVAE to data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP), UK Biobank (UKB), and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we validate its ability to capture known risk factors, such as age and polygenic risk score, on FC-mediated AD risk. We also identify earlier-life modifiable factors including tobacco use, sleep quality, physical activity, and weight/BMI that significantly influence AD risk. Notably, we observe a U-shaped relationship between blood pressure and AD risk, and highlight the brain visual and somatomotor networks as key mediators of risk through FC. Our approach provides a powerful tool for investigating the effect pathways linking early-life interventions to neurodegenerative outcomes, with broad applicability to other brain-related disorders.

papers.abstract_full: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples are central for clinical research and spatial proteomics (SP), yet liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) remains challenging due to protein extraction losses, evaporation during decrosslinking, and inefficient sample preparation. Current methods often involve complex protocols or specialized equipment, limiting scalability, throughput, and proteome depth. We present a streamlined micro-FFPE proteomics protocol for laser-capture microdissection (LMD) that enables high-throughput processing in a 96-well format, completing the workflow from tissue lysis to LC-MS-ready tryptic peptides on Evotips in just 2-hours. By integrating whole-slide imaging, LMD, and narrow-window data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (nDIA-MS), our approach optimizes lysis, decrosslinking, and digestion within nano-wells leveraging the hanging droplet concept. This design minimizes surface adsorption, enhances sample processing efficiency, reduces preparation time by ~30% compared with reference methods, and enables parallel handling of up to 192 samples with standard equipment. This enables the quantification of >5,500 protein groups (PGs) from 50,000 µm² regions (~250 cells), with robust performance down to 1000 µm2 (~5 cells) with ~2,500 PGs identified. Application to breast cancer (BC) tissue resolves BC subtypes and microenvironments via biomarkers (TP53, HER2, PR). Even from ~60 µm² regions of single nuclei identify ~1,800 protein groups, enabling microscale spatial proteomics approaching near-organelle resolution.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Externalizing disorders encompass a range of disinhibited behaviors that typically manifest in youth and are linked with adverse psychological and social outcomes. Polygenic liability to externalizing behaviors has been associated with psychiatric and disease phenotypes in adults. Identifying correlates of genetic risk in youth-prior to the emergence of more impairing manifestations of externalizing behaviors (e.g. substance use disorders)-could improve our etiological understanding and inform targeted prevention efforts. METHODS: We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) to test whether externalizing (EXT) polygenic scores (PGS) were associated with up to 1,697 psychosocial, behavioral, environmental, and health-related phenotypes among youth of European-like genetic ancestry. PheWAS data came from the baseline (n = 4,931, mean age = 9.93 ± 0.63 years, 46.9% female) and two-year follow-up (n = 4,507, 12.02 ± 0.66 years, 47.0% female) data collection waves of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development StudySM (ABCD Study®). Secondary analyses examined within-family effects and moderation by biological sex. RESULTS: EXT PGS was associated with 268 and 352 phenotypes at baseline and follow-up, respectively, following Bonferroni correction at each wave. The strongest associations were observed with externalizing behaviors, screen time/media use, caffeine consumption, sleep disturbances, and poor school performance. Effects were attenuated by 59%-64% within family, on average, with five predominantly externalizing phenotypes remaining significantly associated with within-family PGS. There was limited evidence of moderation by biological sex. CONCLUSIONS: These results broadly characterize the early phenotypic correlates of an externalizing polygenic score and can be used to generate hypotheses about phenotypes that might represent mechanisms or future prevention targets.

This perspective also considers it as a drug-development problem, because diagnostic categories may conceal biological differences relevant to treatment response. papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD) is usually framed as a prescribing problem. This perspective also considers it as a drug-development problem, because diagnostic categories may conceal biological differences relevant to treatment response. SCOPE: We examine five dimensions relevant to psychotropic drug development in TRD: pharmacogenomic variation in exposure, pharmacodynamic target engagement, inflammatory and immunometabolic state, polygenic liability, and anhedonia and reward function. Each is linked to a biological or clinical readout, a development decision, and a medicinal-chemistry implication. Tolerability is treated as a design priority alongside efficacy. We discuss relationships between dimensions, trial design, regulatory requirements, and limitations, distinguishing established exposure tools from candidate predictors of differential treatment benefit. CONCLUSION: Biomarker-informed development could improve the testing of mechanistically targeted treatments, but the integrated framework remains unvalidated. Genotype requires measured exposure, target engagement does not establish clinical efficacy, and candidate response markers require prospective randomized evaluation. Early development should test these assumptions before a marker defines a confirmatory population or prescribing indication.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Whether female reproductive history is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and whether such associations differ between populations, is unclear. We examined age at menarche, parity, and age at first birth in relation to these outcomes in two national cohorts of postmenopausal women in China and the United States. Methods  We analyzed 3,876 women in China postmenopausal at the 2011 examination and 4,357 naturally postmenopausal United States women. Using harmonized definitions, including a modified CKM staging based on the American Heart Association framework, we estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) by modified Poisson regression for CKM stage ≥ 2 (primary), CKM stage ≥ 3, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and tested whether PRs differed between cohorts. Results  Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts (China PR 0.985/year [95% CI 0.974–0.996]; United States 0.982 [0.969–0.995]), but survived correction in the United States only. Later age at first birth was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in the United States (0.991 [0.985–0.996]) but not in China (0.997 [0.992–1.003]). For multimorbidity, later menarche was associated with lower prevalence in the United States (0.919 [0.873–0.967], survived correction), whereas age at first birth showed only a nominal association in China (0.967 [0.940–0.994], not surviving correction). Parity was not associated with any outcome. Conclusions  Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts, with similar magnitude, although this survived correction in the United States only; later age at first birth was associated with lower prevalence in the United States only. For multimorbidity, only later menarche in the United States survived correction. Parity was not associated with any outcome, and no cross-cohort difference survived correction. In these cross-sectional analyses, reproductive history appears to be a life-course marker of modest effect size, warranting prospective evaluation rather than causal or clinical use.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: To evaluate the effect of topical 0.1% tacrolimus on corneal neovascularization (CoNV) and compare its efficacy with 1% prednisolone acetate. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, evaluator-masked, randomized study, patients with CoNV were randomized to 0.1% tacrolimus or 1% prednisolone acetate. Eye drops were administered four times daily for 4 weeks, then twice daily for an additional 4 weeks. Clinical assessments included CoNV grade, visual acuity, intraocular pressure, and ocular surface staining scores. A linear mixed model was used to evaluate treatment effects. RESULTS: Forty-six patients (tacrolimus group, n = 24; prednisolone group, n = 22) were analyzed. Most baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, except for endothelial cell density, which was significantly lower in the tacrolimus group (P = 0.040). In both groups, CoNV grade decreased significantly from baseline to week 4 (tacrolimus group: 2.025 ± 0.162 to 1.733 ± 0.162, P = 0.003; prednisolone group: 1.852 ± 0.168 to 1.625 ± 0.168, P = 0.035), with no significant between-group difference (P = 0.688). No significant change in CoNV grade was observed from week 4 to week 8 in either group. Over the 8-week period, significant within-group decrease in CoNV grade was observed in the tacrolimus group only (2.025 ± 0.162 to 1.697 ± 0.164, P = 0.019). CONCLUSIONS: Both 0.1% tacrolimus and 1% prednisolone acetate reduced CoNV during the first 4 weeks. The sustained reduction in CoNV through 8 weeks in the tacrolimus group suggests its potential as an alternative or adjunctive therapy for CoNV, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have revealed extensive polygenic signals and overlapping genetic architectures across human traits, creating a need for resources that connect trait-level genetic relationships with gene-level functional evidence. Here, we developed the Multi-Omics Causal Resource Database (MOCR-DB), an interactive platform that integrates large-scale GWAS summary statistics from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative with molecular quan…
papers.abstract_full: UNLABELLED: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have revealed extensive polygenic signals and overlapping genetic architectures across human traits, creating a need for resources that connect trait-level genetic relationships with gene-level functional evidence. Here, we developed the Multi-Omics Causal Resource Database (MOCR-DB), an interactive platform that integrates large-scale GWAS summary statistics from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative with molecular quantitative trait locus (QTL) datasets. In total, 613 traits with significant heritability were retained and harmonized using the Unified Medical Language System. MOCR-DB integrates phenotype-to-phenotype analyses, including genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization, with phenotype-to-gene analyses based on QTL-informed summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis (SMR) within a single searchable and interactive framework. The platform supports exploration of cross-trait genetic correlations, putative causal relationships, and candidate functional gene associations. An AI-assisted module provides concise plain-language summaries to help contextualize statistical findings. As a case study, we examined obesity and COVID-19 severity, where genetically predicted obesity showed a stronger association with critical COVID-19 and lung eQTL-based SMR analyses revealed distinct immune- and neuronal-related molecular patterns across severity groups. MOCR-DB thus provides a unified and accessible resource for investigating shared genetic architectures and prioritized functional gene candidates across complex traits, supporting the generation of reproducible and biologically interpretable hypotheses. The database is publicly available at https://chenhongwei.net/public/MOCRdb/. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Data resources, analytical framework, and interpretation in MOCR-DB The Multi-Omics Causal Resource Database (MOCR-DB) integrates large-scale GWAS summary statistics and molecular QTL datasets to provide a unified framework for genetic correlation, causal inference, and functional mediation. Data resources include GWAS summary statistics from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative, together with 53 xQTL datasets across 49 tissues (eQTL, mQTL, sQTL, and caQTL). The analytical framework combines linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) for estimating heritability and cross-trait genetic correlation, Mendelian randomization (MR) to infer potential causal relationships between traits, and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) to identify tissue-specific functional genes. Results are presented through interactive genetic network searches that link diseases, biomarkers, lifestyle factors, and molecular traits via correlation, causality, and functional annotation. An AI-assisted module further facilitates causal and functional interpretation by summarizing complex results from LDSC, MR, and SMR analyses into accessible biological insights. Together, MOCR-DB provides systematic exploration of shared genetic architectures and functional mediators across complex human traits. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43657-026-00338-w.

papers.abstract_full: Background: Recent observational studies suggest that impaired exercise-related heart rate responses may precede the clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD). However, it remains unclear whether this association reflects shared common-variant genetic architecture, bidirectional causal effects, or other mechanisms. Methods: We analyzed genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for post-exercise heart rate recovery at 50 s (N = 54,137), heart rate increase during exercise (N = 54,137), and PD (N = 482,730). Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) estimated genetic correlations (rg). Gene-based, gene-set, and gene-property analyses were conducted using Multi-marker Analysis of GenoMic Annotation (MAGMA) via Functional Mapping and Annotation (FUMA). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal effects. Results: LDSC revealed no significant genetic correlation between PD and post-exercise heart rate recovery at 50 s (rg = -0.006, P = 0.903) or heart rate increase during exercise (rg = -0.021, P = 0.694). No overlap was observed between the sets of genes reaching Bonferroni-corrected significance for PD and either exercise-related heart rate response trait. Likewise, no overlap was observed among significant gene sets or tissue-specific enrichment results after FDR or Bonferroni correction. Bidirectional MR analyses did not identify statistically supported associations within the precision of the available data, with a limited number of instruments and wide confidence intervals. Conclusions: These findings do not support strong shared common-variant genetic architecture or statistically supported bidirectional causal associations between PD and exercise-related heart rate response traits. papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are global health problems that frequently co-occur. The bidirectional causal relationship between them is well established, although the potential mediators remain understudied. Here, we investigated the role of lifestyle and socioeconomic traits as mediators of the MDD-T2D relationship using genetic data. METHODS: Using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, we tested whether the genetic correlation (r g ) between MDD (n = 2,000,702) and T2D (n = 1,812,017) was influenced by lifestyle (physical activity and sedentary time [n = 95,776], cigarettes per day [n = 618,489], and drinks per week [n = 941,280]) and socioeconomic (educational attainment [n = 293,723] and poverty factor [n = 453,689]) traits. Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, using both GWAS and UK Biobank data, were conducted to investigate potential causal relationships. Finally, we applied mediation analysis to quantify the indirect effect of potential mediators. RESULTS: The strong genetic correlation between MDD and T2D (r g = 0.184, p = 3.5 × 10-37) was attenuated when accounting for cigarettes per day (partial r g = 0.098), physical activity (partial r g = 0.141), educational attainment (partial r g = 0.115), and poverty (partial r g = 0.118). MR demonstrated that a higher genetic liability to MDD and T2D was associated with higher cigarettes per day, poverty, and lower education. MR showed that higher education was associated with lower odds of MDD and T2D, while poverty was associated with higher odds of both conditions. Mediation analysis demonstrated that genetic liability to education and poverty traits substantially mediated the causal relationship in both directions: 28.67% and 24.98% for MDD→T2D and 34.3% and 29.87% for T2D→MDD, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the role of socioeconomic traits in the MDD-T2D relationship and demonstrate both the strength and limitations of using MR for investigating complex traits. Further research incorporating gene-environment interactions, policy implications, and diverse populations is needed to better understand this relationship. People with depression are more likely to develop type 2 diabetes (T2D) and vice versa. However, it is unclear how these conditions are linked or which risk factors they share. In this study, we used statistical genetics methods and genetic data from large population studies to investigate whether lifestyle and socioeconomic factors may help explain this relationship. We found that education and poverty partially mediated the relationship between depression and T2D in both directions. These findings highlight the importance of addressing social inequalities alongside clinical care to help reduce the burden of both conditions.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Age-related hearing loss is a common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, with significant public health implications, emphasizing the urgent need for identifying novel therapeutic targets. This study seeks to uncover potential novel therapeutic targets for ARHL by employing proteome-wide Mendelian randomization analysis. METHODS: This investigation employed a proteome-wide Mendelian randomization approach, utilizing publicly accessible data from GWAS and pQTL studies. Additionally, we performed phenome-wide association studies, enrichment analysis, protein network construction, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, colocalization analysis, drug repurposing predictions, and molecular docking simulations, all aimed at identifying more precise and targeted therapeutic strategies. RESULTS: We identified six plasma proteins with genetically predicted causal effects on ARHL risk. GO analysis highlighted their predominant roles in key biological processes, including the regulation of cytosolic calcium ion concentration, negative regulation of homotypic cell-cell adhesion, and regulation of endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response. Additionally, important cellular components include smooth endoplasmic reticulum, and dendritic shaft. Follow-up phenome-wide association, protein network, single-cell transcriptomic, colocalization, drug repurposing, and molecular docking analyses provided convergent evidence supporting EEF2K, C1QTNF1, ATF6, JPH4, KIR2DL3, and MICB as promising therapeutic targets for ARHL, and identified four candidate compounds (Withaferin A, Cianidanol, Danthron, and adenosine triphosphate) for further therapeutic investigation. CONCLUSIONS: Proteome-wide MR identified EEF2K, C1QTNF1, ATF6, JPH4, KIR2DL3, and MICB as candidate therapeutic targets for ARHL, offering new insights into target discovery. Focusing on these proteins may improve target prioritization and enhance the efficiency of drug development for ARHL.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: As generative AI systems increasingly provide answers in everyday and academic contexts, understanding how source attribution influences evaluative judgment has become critical. METHODS: In a within-subjects design, 103 participants evaluated 30 pre-generated reflective-correct, intuitive-incorrect, and arithmetic control-correct answers labeled ChatGPT or computer. Assignment of two parallel batteries to source labels and trial presentation order were randomized, and displays were visually matched. An independent unlabeled pretest with 35 participants supported battery comparability. RESULTS: Participant-level analysis showed greater overall acceptance under ChatGPT (68.0% versus 63.4%, p = 0.002). A trial-level logistic mixed model with crossed participant and parallel-problem-pair random intercepts showed a source-by-category interaction (p < 0.001): acceptance was higher under ChatGPT for arithmetic controls (OR = 6.08, 95% CI [2.70, 13.69]), while source contrasts within the two CRT categories were not significant. Judgment accuracy is reported descriptively. Signal-detection analyses of CRT answers detected no significant source difference in sensitivity (p = 0.930) or criterion (p = 0.082). Evaluation times were longer under ChatGPT in the raw-time analysis (p = 0.034), but the source difference was not significant after log transformation (p = 0.180). Exploratory correlations detected no significant associations between source-related differences and trust, AI attitudes, or critical-thinking disposition. DISCUSSION: These findings distinguish overall source-related endorsement, particularly for arithmetic controls, from successful discrimination between correct and incorrect CRT answers.

papers.abstract: Background Circulating immune proteins represent an important class of therapeutic targets, but existing proteome-wide genetic studies have not systematically resolved immune-related target-disease relationships across a broad disease phenome within a unified framework that integrates causal inference, locus colocalization, orthogonal protein-level support, independent replication, and standardized evidence grading. papers.abstract_full: Background Circulating immune proteins represent an important class of therapeutic targets, but existing proteome-wide genetic studies have not systematically resolved immune-related target-disease relationships across a broad disease phenome within a unified framework that integrates causal inference, locus colocalization, orthogonal protein-level support, independent replication, and standardized evidence grading. Methods We developed the Human Plasma Immune Atlas (HPIA), a tiered proteogenomic framework built from public datasets. We curated 1,007 plasma immune proteins from 2,923 Olink Explore analytes, instrumented each encoding gene with its strongest blood cis-expression quantitative trait locus (eQTLGen), and tested effects on 2,469 FinnGen R12 disease endpoints by Mendelian randomization (MR), followed by colocalization, protein-level validation with INTERVAL cis-protein quantitative trait loci, 2-population replication in UK Biobank, and prespecified 5-tier evidence grading. A companion Plasma Immune Risk Score (PIRS; elastic-net Cox) is released for predicting targets. Results Across 1,656,872 evaluable gene-disease tests, 1,016 associations involving 220 immune genes and 381 diseases met FDR < 0.05, of which 417 showed strong evidence of colocalization (PP.H4 ≥ 0.80). Positive-control analyses recapitulated five established immune drug-target relationships and the ACE-hypertension relationship with directionally concordant genetic effects. Among 189 discovery associations evaluable in UK Biobank, 162 (86%) showed concordant effect directions and 89 met the prespecified replication criterion. Cardiovascular phenotypes contained the largest number of high-confidence associations, accounting for 67 of 176 core target-disease pairs, while hypertension was associated with 28 immune proteins. Integration of MR, colocalization, protein-level evidence, and replication promoted five target-disease pairs to the highest evidence tier, including ANXA2-hypertension and PPP3R1-venous/lymphatic disease. Systematic prioritization further identified 45 colocalized candidate therapeutic target-indication pairs with genetically inferred directions of intervention. In validation evaluation, the PIRS achieved a cross-validated concordance index of 0.777. Conclusions HPIA provides an open, genetics-anchored map connecting the circulating immune system to the human disease phenome and distinguishes initial genetic associations from target-disease relationships supported by orthogonal evidence. The framework identifies cardiovascular phenotypes as a major concentration of genetically supported immune associations and provides experimentally testable hypotheses for therapeutic target discovery, drug repurposing, and immune-informed disease stratification.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: The availability of health guidance (AHG) provided by general practitioners (GPs) may vary in complex primary care settings. This study aimed to assess the AHG for patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in general practice setting and examine the association between AHG and the patients' diabetes self-management activities. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in seven community health service centers (CHSCs) in Beijing, China. Data on patient and GP characteristics, perceived AHG, and self-management measured by the Summary Diabetes Self-Care Activities (SDSCA) were collected through questionnaire surveys. The AHG included accessibility of health guidance from a GP and AHG on diet, exercise, psychological support, hypoglycemia prevention, and complication identification. A two-level generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was used to examine the association between the AHG and diabetes self-management considering both patient- and GP-level characteristics. RESULTS: A total of 28 GPs and 716 patients were recruited. The mean AHG score was 3.97 ± 1.84 (range: 0-6). Among AHG domains, complication identification guidance showed the poorest availability (40.5%). AHG was significantly associated with diabetes self-management activities (P < 0.001). In the GLMM, higher AHG scores remained associated with better self-management activities after adjustment for both patient- and GP-level factors. In addition, T2DM duration of more than 10 years was positively associated with self-management activities, while the presence of comorbidities was negatively associated with self-management activities. CONCLUSIONS: Perceived GP-provided health guidance was significantly associated with self-management activities among patients with T2DM in primary care settings. Improving the capacity of GP-led primary care teams and promoting the active participation of team members in delivering individualized and comprehensive health guidance may contribute to better self-management activities among patients with T2DM and enhance the effectiveness of diabetes management in primary care.

papers.abstract_full: Fine-mapping methods based on summary statistics from genome-wide association studies and linkage disequilibrium (LD) information are widely used to identify potential causal variants. However, LD mismatch between the external LD reference panel and the genome-wide association study population is common and can compromise fine-mapping accuracy. Here we developed Robust SparsePro (RSparsePro), a probabilistic graphical model with an efficient variational inference algorithm, to perform robust fine-mapping in the presence of LD mismatch. In simulation studies with varying degrees of LD mismatch, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher power and coverage than existing methods. In fine-mapping cis-protein quantitative trait loci and complex trait risk loci, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher enrichment of variants with potential functional impacts and cross-study and cross-LD-reference-panel replication rates. RSparsePro also identified biologically relevant variants in drug target genes and implicated potential regulatory mechanisms for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.

papers.abstract_full: Genetic effects on gene expression often vary across cell types, motivating expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Existing approaches generally aggregate expression across cells, use Gaussian models poorly suited to read counts or do not scale. Here we show that SAIGE-QTL, a Poisson mixed model that directly models single-cell read counts, enables calibrated and computationally scalable eQTL mapping while accounting for donor-level and cell-level covariates and unequal numbers of cells per donor. In simulations and three single-cell datasets, SAIGE-QTL improved statistical efficiency and discovery of genes with significant eQTLs (eGenes) relative to pseudobulk methods and produced results consistent with existing single-cell models at substantially lower computational cost. In 1.2 million immune cells, SAIGE-QTL identified 48.8% more eGenes than pseudobulk analysis. SAIGE-QTL further enabled genome-wide trans-eQTL mapping and rare variant set-based testing, identifying rare variant associations independent of common eQTL signals. SAIGE-QTL therefore expands single-cell eQTL discovery across common, rare and trans-acting genetic variation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Erysipelas is an acute skin and soft-tissue infection predominantly caused by streptococci, yet the host genetic architecture and non-coding regulatory mechanisms underlying susceptibility remain poorly characterized. We integrated FinnGen R11 erysipelas GWAS data (24,825 cases and 399,149 controls) with GTEx v8 and multiple functional genomic resources. Cross-tissue and tissue-specific TWAS, MAGMA, and Polygenic Priority Score (PoPS) analyses were combined with regional association testing, functional annotation, eQTL/sQTL and colocalization analyses, ENCODE chromatin annotations, rE2G/ABC enhancer-to-gene mapping, and AlphaGenome, Borzoi, and Enformer sequence-to-function models. TNRC6B was the only gene remaining significant after FDR correction in UTMOST (P = 1.21 × 10⁻⁵, FDR = 0.045) and was further supported by FUSION, MAGMA (Z = 3.4697, P = 2.61 × 10⁻⁴), and PoPS (score = 0.7712; genome-wide rank 324/18,383; local rank 2/31). No regional variant reached genome-wide significance. Integrated regulatory analyses prioritized rs4821940 and rs6001827 as Tier A candidates, whereas the 3′UTR variant rs139915 was classified as Tier B. Sequence-to-function models provided context-dependent support, although effect directions varied across models and tissues. Evidence-module integration, leave-one-module-out analyses, and 5,000 random weight perturbations consistently ranked rs4821940, rs6001827, and rs139915 among the top three candidates. These findings prioritize TNRC6B and linked regulatory variants for further investigation but do not establish causal effects.

papers.abstract: Recent transcriptome-wide association studies (TWASs) of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia have identified risk genes whose effects are potentially mediated through gene expression, but most do not consider other transcriptomic regulatory modalities that may contribute to AD genetic risk. To address this gap, we profiled transcriptomic quantitative traits across six modalities––gene expression, RNA stability, isoform ratios, splice junction usage, alternative TSS and polyA usage––from dorsolater…
papers.abstract_full: Recent transcriptome-wide association studies (TWASs) of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia have identified risk genes whose effects are potentially mediated through gene expression, but most do not consider other transcriptomic regulatory modalities that may contribute to AD genetic risk. To address this gap, we profiled transcriptomic quantitative traits across six modalities––gene expression, RNA stability, isoform ratios, splice junction usage, alternative TSS and polyA usage––from dorsolateral prefrontal cortex RNA-seq data tissue (n=1,035). We profiled 396,344 transcriptomic traits, which we leveraged for quantitative trait loci (xQTL) mapping and TWAS analyses of AD. We identified 25,736 xGenes (49.6% of analyzed genes) with at least one conditionally independent xQTL in separate-modality mapping, increasing signal detection by 42% relative to studying expression alone. Cross-modality mapping reduced redundant independent xQTLs by 45% while retaining signals better aligned with biological characteristics of each modality. We colocalized cross-modality xQTLs with 55 of 75 AD GWAS risk loci, including 15 risk loci detected only with non-expression modalities. TWAS analyses identified 161 independent risk genes with 59% detected through non-expression modalities and ∼30% in multiple modalities. Follow-up proteome-wide association studies using DLPFC proteomic data provided proteomic support for 26 of these independent xTWAS risk genes. Protein–protein interaction analysis further showed that 46.6% of these independent xTWAS risk genes form an interconnected network through hub genes including  MAPT, BIN1, and  TREM2 . Our study demonstrates that studying transcriptional modalities besides expression substantially enhances the detection of AD-associated genetic signals and elucidates their underlying mechanisms.

papers.abstract_full: Population DNA methylome analyses remain largely confined to reference-defined genomic space despite extensive human genetic diversity. A central challenge is therefore to define comparable methylation phenotypes across diverse genomes and map the genetic architecture of methylome variation. Here, using 460 haplotypes from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2, we develop two complementary pangenome-based frameworks: one compares methylation within homologous regions while retaining haplotype-specific structural configuration and CpG content; the other represents CpG island (CGI) variation at homologous loci as sequence-resolved alleles. We identified 47,039 CGI alleles, including 8,040 absent from CHM13; 62% were attributable to structural variants and 31% to small variants. Through local genealogies, we reconstructed CGI gain, loss and turnover, revealing how present-day methylation differences align with CGI evolutionary trajectories. We found that genome-wide, methylation variability was buffered against genetic diversity across more than 90% of the genome, with exceptions at extreme nucleotide diversity and locally around structural variants. Our methylation framework enabled population-scale allele-aware methylation quantitative trait locus (mQTL) mapping into non-reference and structurally complex sequence, where mQTL-associated intervals were enriched. mQTLs linked methylation to transcriptomic phenotypes, population differentiation and complex traits, supporting 8% of population differentially methylated regions and colocalizing with more than half of genome-wide association study loci. Together, our study redefines human methylome analysis and our findings reveal a genome-wide architecture of genetic-epigenetic coupling, reshaping how methylation variation is interpreted across human development and disease.

This study integrated multi-environment phenotyping with 1.75 million SNPs derived from whole genome resequencing of 172 cultivated  Sorghum bicolor  and  S. bicolor  ×  S. halepense  derivative lines evaluated across temperate …
papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Improving crop productivity per unit of water and nitrogen is central to climate resilient sorghum improvement, yet the genetic architecture of biomass-based resource productivity remains poorly resolved across contrasting production environments. This study integrated multi-environment phenotyping with 1.75 million SNPs derived from whole genome resequencing of 172 cultivated  Sorghum bicolor  and  S. bicolor  ×  S. halepense  derivative lines evaluated across temperate Mediterranean and semi-arid tropical environments. Results  Biomass-based water productivity and partial factor productivity of applied nitrogen displayed extensive genetic variation and high broad-sense heritability of 0.75 to 0.81, whereas grain-based indices were more strongly influenced by genotype × environment interaction. Multi-model genome wide association analyses identified 27 significant SNPs defining 22 genomic regions for biomass-based productivity. A recurrent chromosome 9 signal at S09_55037491 was detected across three analytical models and biomass-derived indices and colocalized with Sobic.009G200500, a nitrate-responsive HAT3.1 homeobox transcription factor. Haplotype analysis independently prioritized two additional loci: a chromosome 9 haplotype associated with a 2.7-fold difference in biomass-based water productivity and containing an AHP-like cytokinin-signaling gene, and a chromosome 5 haplotype associated with a 1.86-fold difference and encompassing DAD1, a phospholipase implicated in jasmonate biosynthesis. Candidate gene prioritization also implicated aquaporin-mediated transport, trehalose-6-phosphate metabolism, oxidative signaling and, provisionally, C4 carbon assimilation. Most favorable common haplotypes occurred within cultivated germplasm rather than the introgressed lines. Conclusions  Together, these findings reveal genetically tractable loci and biological pathways underlying sorghum biomass productivity per unit of supplied water and nitrogen. Following independent validation, the identified SNPs and haplotypes could support diagnostic marker development and haplotype informed selection, while genomic selection remains more appropriate for environmentally sensitive grain-based productivity traits.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Psychiatric nurses manage aggression, interrupted recovery and emotionally demanding care. Surveys quantify distress but rarely show how these experiences accumulate during routine work. AIM: We aimed to estimate the prevalence of a positive depressive-symptom screen among psychiatric nurses and to quantify its associations with four prespecified occupational exposures: workplace violence, night-shift burden, occupational strain and psychological resilience. A longitudinal qualitative phase then examined how nurses experienced these same exposures during routine work. METHODS: Four tertiary public psychiatric hospitals in northern Jiangsu participated from January 2025 to March 2026. A convenience sample of 357 nurses completed the survey. Workplace violence during the preceding 12 months was assessed with Wang's Workplace Violence Scale; at least one physical, verbal or psychological, or sexual incident perpetrated by a psychiatric inpatient or visiting family member defined exposure. Modified Poisson regression with hospital fixed effects estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) for an SDS-positive screen. A purposive subsample of 20 nurses completed interviews, diaries and observation over three months. Colaizzi's method and a joint display supported qualitative analysis and integration. RESULTS: Of 357 nurses, 138 (38.7%) screened positive. Nurses reporting violence had a higher screening prevalence (PR 1.65, 95% CI 1.31-2.08). PRs per SD were 1.48 (95% CI 1.33-1.66) for night-shift burden and 1.45 (95% CI 1.28-1.65) for occupational strain. Resilience showed the opposite pattern (PR 0.79 per SD, 95% CI 0.70-0.88). Qualitative accounts centered on repeated strain, a value-recognition mismatch, unequal recovery resources and support considered generic or poorly timed. CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms were common. Nurses identified practical targets: safer work organization, rapid post-incident contact and support tailored to individual circumstances. Cross-sectional estimates do not establish diagnosis or causation.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Online panels use panel-registered sex (PRS) for sampling and quota control. PRS may not align with questionnaire-based sex assigned at birth (SAB). We examined whether PRS-SAB discordance was associated with quality-control (QC) exclusion. METHODS: We analyzed all 32,000 respondents before QC exclusion in a Japanese internet survey conducted in 2022. Discordance was defined as non-alignment between binary PRS and SAB, including SAB responses other than male or female. QC criteria comprised household size ≥ 15, attention-check failure, or straight-lining in comorbidity or alcohol/substance-use items. Modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with sequential adjustment for survey-design variables, respondent characteristics, and prior QC-exclusion history. RESULTS: Overall, 918 respondents (2.9%) were PRS-SAB discordant. QC exclusion was more frequent among discordant than concordant respondents (24.2% vs 10.1%). The crude PR was 2.39 (95% CI, 2.12-2.69) and the adjusted PR was 1.74 (95% CI, 1.52-1.98). The association persisted after excluding first-time respondents and in sensitivity analyses restricting SAB or gender identity responses. CONCLUSION: QC procedures may reduce the representation of respondents with sex/gender-related measure discordance. Researchers should not treat PRS as interchangeable with questionnaire-based SAB and should assess whether QC exclusion alters sex/gender-related sample composition.

papers.abstract: Extracellular matrix (ECM) components that transmit mechanical loads are ubiquitous in the mammalian body. Collagen, the primary structural component of most ECMs, is present throughout connective tissues (CTs) and forms a continuous fibrous scaffold that joins ECMs and extends from the epidermis to the bone marrow. papers.abstract_full: Extracellular matrix (ECM) components that transmit mechanical loads are ubiquitous in the mammalian body. Collagen, the primary structural component of most ECMs, is present throughout connective tissues (CTs) and forms a continuous fibrous scaffold that joins ECMs and extends from the epidermis to the bone marrow. Within each ECM, both fibrillar collagen and the interposed glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) and proteoglycans (PGs), which bind and retain water, dynamically adapt to functional requirements. In this review, we describe how type I and III fibrillar collagens, which are the predominant collagens found in the body, form fibrils of different sizes, structures, and orientations that allow them to resist and transmit tensile forces from the environment to the deeper bone marrow, and, in some tissues, to resist compressive loads. These collagen types are embedded within a viscous matrix of GAGs and PGs that mainly oppose compressive loads and further contribute to the mechanical and functional properties of the continuous collagen network. These factors are consistent with a theoretical model emphasizing a broad role for ECM systems in sensing, adapting, and transmitting external mechanical stimuli from the epidermis to the bone marrow, allowing these signals to act across the basement membrane, dermis, hypodermis, fascia superficialis, subcutaneous tissue, deep fascia, muscle sheaths, tendon, ligament, periosteum, bone, and endosteum.

papers.abstract_full: Functional data are widely collected across many fields. One approach for modeling functional data collected across repeated measures is longitudinal functional PCA (LFPCA), which allows for the decomposition of variability at multiple levels. However, existing estimation approaches for LFPCA can be computationally demanding for large or high-dimensional datasets. Here, we propose fast generalized LFPCA, a novel estimation technique that bins data along the functional domain and fits a marginal mixed model at each bin. Simulation results show that the proposed method is orders of magnitude faster than existing techniques while achieving similar accuracy, making LFPCA scalable to datasets with more densely sampled observations and larger sample sizes. We apply the proposed technique to model neuronal firing rate data both on and off deep brain stimulation (DBS) to investigate how the intervention modulates populationlevel neuronal activity. Our results suggest that the vast majority of between-neuron variation can be explained by four principal components, which relate to individual differences in neuronal firing as well as the arm manipulation paradigm under study. We also find that DBS significantly increases the variability of firing activity, likely driven by increased firing from a subset of neurons in response to DBS, a novel insight not obtained in previous analyses. Code to implement the proposed method and run simulation studies is included in the supplement.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) is a highly metastatic and invasive malignancy. Keratin 5 (KRT5) and serine protease inhibitor B5 (SERPINB5/Maspin) have been reported to play crucial roles in various cancers; however, their interaction and the underlying molecular mechanisms in melanoma remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the functional roles of KRT5 and SERPINB5 in melanoma progression and elucidate the mechanisms underlying their synergistic effects. METHODS: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in SKCM was performed using the STRING database. Hub genes were identified via Cytoscape, and their interactions and colocalization were validated by immunofluorescence (IF) and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). In A375 cells, the effects of KRT5 and SERPINB5 on cellular phenotypes were evaluated via overexpression (oe-KRT5, oe-SERPINB5) and p53 knockdown (sh-p53). Functional assays-including wound healing, Transwell, cell-matrix adhesion, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation, and flow cytometry-were employed to assess cell cycle distribution and apoptosis. Changes in key p53 signaling pathways and downstream molecules were detected via Western Blot and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). RESULTS: PPI network analysis identified KRT5 and SERPINB5 as key hub genes. IF and Co-IP experiments confirmed their direct molecular interaction in A375 cells. Functionally, KRT5/SERPINB5 co-expression synergistically inhibited cell migration, invasion, cell-matrix adhesion, and proliferation while inducing G1 cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Mechanistically, their co-expression specifically activated the p53 signaling pathway; p53 knockdown reversed the functional phenotypes induced by KRT5/SERPINB5 co-expression. Further mechanistic studies revealed that KRT5/SERPINB5 downregulated the cell cycle-related genes cyclin A2 (CCNA2) and cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) and upregulated the expression of cell adhesion molecule E-cadherin (CDH1) through p53 activation. CONCLUSIONS: KRT5 and SERPINB5 synergistically activate the p53 pathway, modulate downstream gene networks involved in cell cycle and adhesion, and thereby exert cooperative tumor-suppressive effects by inhibiting cell-matrix adhesion, migration, and invasion, as well as inducing cell cycle arrest.

papers.abstract_full: Background We evaluated patient-level factors associated with the interval from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy and list-level factors associated with overrun in elective gynaecology lists. Methods This retrospective observational study used 2025 nursing pre-assessment and theatre timing records from two hospitals within one National Health Service (NHS) trust. Duration was analysed using a lognormal mixed model with a theatre-list random intercept, adjusting for recorded pre-assessment characteristics, session, site, and mixed-list status. Body mass index (BMI) was modelled using a four-knot restricted cubic spline. Adjusted mean differences were reported in minutes. Secondary analyses used mixed-effects logistic regression for intervals ≥22 minutes and multivariable logistic regression for list overrun, defined as last-patient departure after the scheduled finish. Sensitivity analyses examined untransformed duration and excluded all-day lists. Results Among 913 hysteroscopies, 890 cases across 491 theatre lists were included in adjusted analyses. BMI was nonlinearly associated with duration (overall p<0.001; nonlinearity p=0.007). Compared with BMI 30 kg/m², adjusted mean intervals were 1.42 minutes longer (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.46-2.43) at 40 kg/m² and 4.67 minutes longer (95% CI 2.56-6.90) at 50 kg/m². These contrasts were similar in sensitivity analyses. Among 611 gynaecology lists, 302 (49.4%) overran. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun than lists containing only minor procedures (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 3.10; 95% CI 2.00-4.80). Afternoon lists had lower odds than morning lists (OR 0.23; 95% CI 0.15-0.34), while odds were higher at University Hospital Lewisham than Queen Elizabeth Hospital (OR 2.18; 95% CI 1.49-3.20). Lists in which at least half of minor cases had prolonged intervals also had higher odds of overrun (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.04-2.23), but evidence for this association was less certain after excluding all-day lists (OR 1.40; 95% CI 0.92-2.11). Conclusions Higher BMI was associated with longer intervals from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun. Prospective studies should evaluate whether accounting for preparation requirements and list composition improves scheduling. These findings do not establish a BMI threshold or booking rule.

In contrast, survival of alkaline stress favors smaller cells and is transiently heritable: co-survival probability remains high among relatives separated by up to two generations. papers.abstract_full: Single-molecule localisation microscopy (SMLM) is a powerful tool in molecular and cellular biology and part of the broad umbrella of super-resolution microscopy. A distinct feature of SMLM, is its capacity for deep quantification, beyond just spatial information, to copy number, stoichiometry, molecular interaction and dynamics in living cells. The hardware required is increasingly straightforward to implement. However, complexity remains in the image analysis where much remains fragmented across specialised software tools. Here, we present MaCADEMIA (Matlab Computational Analysis of Diffusion, Emitter Molecular Intensity and Abundance), a simple yet powerful toolbox of MATLAB functions and associated documentation to enable straightforward extraction of quantitative single-molecule information. MaCADEMIA performs ensemble particle detection achieving localisation accuracies down to 0.5 pixels Root mean squared error (RMSE) across wide signal-to-noise (SNR) ranges on standardised particle tracking benchmarks, consistently matching or exceeding the performance of 14 leading methods. Our integrated workflow enables molecular counting and stoichiometry determination through stepwise photobleaching analysis, mobility measurement via mean squared displacement, colocalisaton analysis and absolute protein copy number quantification using three-dimensional cellular models.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Phycocyanobilin (PCB) is a linear tetrapyrrolic chromophore derived from C-phycocyanin with reported antioxidant and neuroprotective properties. However, its cellular uptake and intracellular distribution in neuronal cells remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize PCB internalization in PC12 cells and to examine its spatial association with DHE- and JC-1-positive intracellular regions. Methods PC12 cells were incubated with PCB at 25 or 100 μM for different time periods. Cellular uptake and accumulation were evaluated by confocal microscopy (CFM) and flow cytometry. Intracellular spatial association of PCB with DHE- and JC-1-positive regions was assessed by colocalization analysis using Pearson’s coefficient, Manders’ coefficients, Intensity Correlation Quotient (ICQ), and Costes randomization analysis. Results PCB was progressively internalized by PC12 cells and accumulated predominantly in cytoplasmic and perinuclear regions in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. CFM and flow cytometry showed strong concordance, with significant correlations for the percentage of PCB-positive cells (r = 0.8603, p = 0.0061) and fluorescence intensity (r = 0.9563, p = 0.0002). PCB showed substantial spatial overlap with DHE-positive regions, with high Manders’ coefficients (M1 = 0.99; M2 = 0.91) and positive ICQ values. Spatial association was also observed with JC-1-positive regions, although Pearson coefficients indicated a weaker linear intensity correlation than that observed with DHE. Conclusions PCB is efficiently internalized by PC12 cells and exhibits time- and concentration-dependent intracellular accumulation. Its spatial association with DHE- and JC-1-positive regions provides preliminary evidence linking intracellular PCB distribution to cellular regions relevant to redox and mitochondrial biology. Further studies using organelle-specific markers and functional assays are required to establish the mechanistic significance of these spatial associations.
bullets: Conclusions PCB is efficiently internalized by PC12 cells and exhibits time- and concentration-dependent intracellular accumulation.
Its spatial association with DHE- and JC-1-positive regions provides preliminary evidence linking intracellular PCB distribution to cellular regions relevant to redox and mitochondrial biology.
Further studies using organelle-specific markers and functional assays are required to establish the mechanistic significance of these spatial associations.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Biological risk scores provide objective markers of bipolar disorder (BD) liability. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have led to polygenic risk scores (PRSs) that capture genetic liability to BD at the individual level. We lack a comparable large-scale effort to leverage a brain-wide association study (BWAS) to create an imaging risk score (IRS) that captures brain structural liability to BD at the individual-level. Here, we conduct the largest multivariate BWAS of BD and develop a BD IRS. We compare the BD IRS to the PRS and assess their combined predictive performance in multimodal risk score (MRS) models. METHODS: Our multivariate BD BWAS used 153 structural neuroimaging features from 3902 cases and 6855 controls (mean age (sd)=35.47 years (13.42), 56.70% female) in a cross-validated machine learning approach. Using the resulting model coefficients, we constructed an IRS. We then evaluated the out-of-sample performance of the IRS, PRS derived from the largest GWAS to date, and combined MRS model using logistic regression in a subset of individuals with imaging and genetic data (n BD =486, n controls =1701, age (sd)=33.10 (12.02), 56.47% female). We also performed stratified analyses for demographic and BD clinical groups. Prediction performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Subsequent analyses examined associations between each risk score and BD relevant symptoms in developing youth. OUTCOMES: In predicting case status, the BD BWAS model achieved a mean AUC BD of 0.62 (sd BD =0.08) and in stratified analyses, had higher prediction than subgroup-specific BWAS models. The BD type II BWAS was the only exception (AUC BDII =0.60, sd BDII =0.07 vs AUC BD =0.58, sd BD =0.09). The BD PRS had an AUC BD of 0.65 (CI 95% =0.63-0.68) and a higher AUC than subtype-specific PRS in stratified analyses. The PRS typically attained a higher AUC than the IRS. Notably, the IRS and PRS were uncorrelated (r=0.03, p=0.11). MRS models outperformed the prediction of individual PRS and IRS with the strongest prediction for BD type I (AUC BD =0.74, CI 95% =0.70-0.78). The IRS had the strongest associations with BD-related symptoms in developing youth including increased energy (OR=1.21, p fdr =0.03) and distress from psychotic-like experiences (OR=1.23, p fdr =0.04). INTERPRETATION: Our BD IRS is a novel biological indicator of BD risk. The lack of correlation between the IRS and PRS along with improved MRS prediction suggests the two risk scores capture some orthogonal liability to BD. We show that integrating imaging and genetics is useful for biological characterization of BD and should be considered for the development of clinically relevant prediction models.

The lack of correlation between the IRS and PRS along with improved MRS prediction suggests the two risk scores capture some orthogonal liability to BD.
We show that integrating imaging and genetics is useful for biological characterization of BD and should be considered for the development of clinically relevant prediction models.

papers.abstract_full: Polygenic scores for major depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder have been related to treatment outcome. We analysed 4,007 patients of European ancestry from 7 cohorts: three with major depression (STAR*D, GSRD, PANDORA), two with bipolar disorder (STEP-BD, Barcelona) and two with schizophrenia (CATIE, HSRRm). The three scores were computed with PRS-CS from the latest Psychiatric Genomics Consortium studies. The primary outcome was good response or good course, harmonized from each cohort's instrument. Firth logistic regression within cohorts, adjusted for age, sex and ancestry components, was followed by random-effects pooling. A higher depression score was associated with lower odds of a good outcome (odds ratio per standard deviation 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.99, p = .04; false discovery rate q = .11). The estimate remained below one in all 8 sensitivity analyses, including adjustment for baseline severity, and was negative in all 5 cohorts with a continuous improvement measure. The schizophrenia score pointed the same way (odds ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.85-1.01) with no heterogeneity. The bipolar score showed no pooled effect (odds ratio 0.97), and its direction differed by diagnosis. In pooled data spanning three diagnoses, higher polygenic liability to depression was nominally associated with a less favourable treatment outcome, although the association did not survive correction for multiple testing; schizophrenia liability showed a similar directional trend. These findings support further evaluation of disorder liability in multivariable models of treatment outcome.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: The Schizophrenia Exome Meta-Analysis (SCHEMA) Consortium has recently identified 40 genes at a false discovery rate <0.05 in which ultra-rare damaging variants substantially increase schizophrenia (SZ) risk. However, the impact of these variants on clinical trajectories across the psychosis spectrum is not yet known. METHODS: We screened 9,821 sequenced participants with psychotic disorders who passed genomic quality control from the SUPER-Finland psychosis study for ultra-rare variants predicted to be damaging in these 40 SZ-associated genes, identifying 163 variant carriers. To assess the impact of these variants on clinical course and functioning across psychotic disorders, we used five decades of nationwide, full-coverage health register data together with interview, questionnaire, and cognitive assessments collected at study enrollment. We compared the clinical trajectories and functional outcomes of these variant carriers with those of non-carriers, including comparisons across different strata of the schizophrenia polygenic risk score (SZ-PGS) and with participants harboring deleterious variants in other genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). RESULTS: Overall, the variant carriers had a similar distribution of major psychotic disorder diagnoses to that of non-carriers. Despite this diagnostic similarity, variant carriers had earlier hospital admissions than non-carriers for both psychiatric (HR=2.30 [1.48-3.57], p=2.05e-04) and non-psychiatric diagnoses (HR=1.40 [1.10-1.79], p=6.88e-03), indicating increased medical needs early in life. They also showed greater exposure to childhood adversity, lower attainment of adult social milestones, and poorer neuropsychological test performance at study inclusion. Across longitudinal measures, variant carriers showed less favorable clinical and functional trajectories than non-carriers and clustered more closely with individuals with high SZ-PGS (≥90th percentile). Consistent with a liability-threshold model, the variant carriers had lower SZ-PGS than non-carriers among participants with a diagnosis of SZ (β = -0.40, p = 5.32e-05) but higher SZ-PGS than population controls (β = 0.55, p = 9.36e-08), suggesting that the variant carriers developed psychosis at lower levels of common-variant liability. Gene-level analyses identified associations of variants in AKAP11, SETD1A, and XPO7 with lower SZ-PGS and/or poorer neuropsychological test performance, while carriers of damaging variants in SZ-risk genes also associated with bipolar disorder showed high cumulative burdens of affective disorder diagnoses. CONCLUSION: The disease trajectories of carriers of ultra-rare damaging variants in SZ-risk genes broadly overlapped with those of non-carriers, but carriers showed several differences: greater childhood adversity, earlier hospitalizations, and poorer neuropsychological test performance. These carrier-associated differences were detectable across psychotic disorder diagnoses and suggest a broader phenotypic impact of rare SZ-risk variants than is captured by SZ diagnosis alone, with potential clinical relevance for future risk stratification and genetic counseling.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease may occur without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs), but the frequency and angiographic phenotype of such presentations in South Asian catheterization cohorts remain uncertain. We estimated registry-defined SMuRF-less frequency, tested alternative dyslipidaemia definitions, and compared angiographic phenotypes by SMuRF status. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, registry-based cross-sectional analysis of 51,864 admissions with matched catheterization records at a Bangladeshi tertiary cardiac centre from 2005 to 2024. Admissions were classified as SMuRF-less when no qualifying hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or dyslipidaemia was documented or identified; dyslipidaemia reflected a documented diagnosis or qualifying lipid measurement. Documented-only and statin-inclusive definitions were sensitivity analyses. We calculated unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Under the primary definition, 3172 admissions (6.1%) were SMuRF-less, compared with 6.5% under the documented-only definition and 1.6% under the statin-inclusive definition. Among admissions with a classifiable angiographic phenotype, SMuRF-less admissions more frequently had normal coronary arteries (24.9% vs. 10.7%; PR, 2.34; 95% CI, 2.18-2.50) and less frequently had obstructive coronary artery disease (56.6% vs. 71.2%; PR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.77-0.82). Among admissions with obstructive disease, multivessel disease was less frequent (49.6% vs. 57.8%; PR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.82-0.90), whereas recorded intracoronary thrombus was more frequent (5.3% vs. 3.2%; PR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.33-2.04). Of 6635 ST-elevation myocardial infarction admissions, 355 (5.4%) were SMuRF-less; 318 (89.6%) had obstructive disease. CONCLUSION: Registry-defined SMuRF-less admissions, reflecting absence of documented qualifying factors rather than prospectively verified biological absence, were uncommon, and their estimated frequency depended on risk-factor ascertainment. Although their recorded angiographic burden was generally lower, obstructive disease remained common, particularly in ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The absence of documented SMuRFs should not provide clinical reassurance. Prospective patient-level studies with standardized risk-factor assessment and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Dyslipidemia is a known contributor to hypertension, yet the utility of the non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHHR) for hypertension assessment remains unclear. We examined whether the NHHR is associated with hypertension and whether this association varies by demographic and metabolic characteristics. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 10,735 adults who underwent health examinations. Participants were grouped by NHHR quartiles. Modified Poisson regression was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) for the association between NHHR and hypertension. RESULTS: Hypertension was present in 32.8% of participants. Each one-unit increase in NHHR was not significantly associated with hypertension in the unadjusted model (PR 0.99, 95% CI 0.96-1.03, P = 0.735). After adjustment for age, sex, and eGFR, the association became significant (PR 1.09, 95% CI 1.05-1.12, P < 0.001), with participants in the highest quartile having 24% higher prevalence compared with the lowest (PR 1.24, 95% CI 1.13-1.37, P < 0.001). However, after additional adjustment for BMI, the association was substantially attenuated (PR 1.03, 95% CI 1.00-1.07, P = 0.068). These findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: An elevated NHHR was associated with hypertension after adjustment for demographic factors, but this association was substantially attenuated by BMI, suggesting that adiposity largely accounts for the observed relationship. The NHHR may serve as a convenient lipid-related marker, but its clinical utility for screening requires further investigation.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy, parental leave, and lactation remain challenging for surgical trainees, yet specialty-specific data in plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) are limited. This study evaluates resident and faculty experiences and perceptions to identify gaps between faculty beliefs and resident lived experiences surrounding parenthood and postpartum return to work. METHODS: Cross-sectional surveys were distributed to plastic surgery residents and faculty through the American Council of Educators in Plastic Surgery. Resident surveys assessed parental leave, lactation practices, and postpartum experiences. Faculty surveys examined attitudes toward resident pumping, perceived workflow impact, and institutional culture. Descriptive analyzes were performed. RESULTS: 34 residents and 54 faculty completed the survey, for response rates of 30.1 and 10.7%, respectively. Residents reported longer parental leave (mean 8.1 weeks) than faculty had during their own training (5.3 weeks), yet many still relied on vacation or elective time. Although 90.7% of faculty strongly supported resident lactation needs and 79.6% believed their institution fostered a supportive culture, 62.5% of lactating residents stopped breastfeeding earlier than intended, citing insufficient time, distant lactation spaces, and pressure to maintain workflow. One-quarter felt uncomfortable pumping around faculty, and over one-third experienced lactation-related medical complications. Postpartum mood symptoms (55.6%) and guilt (63.6%) were also prevalent among trainees. CONCLUSIONS: Disparities persist between faculty and resident perceptions of parental leave and lactation support during residency training. Improving parenthood in plastic surgery requires coordinated infrastructure, support for flexible lactation practices, policy enforcement and promotion, and cultural change. Aligning policy, practice, and expectations is essential to support resident well-being, promote equity, and strengthen the plastic surgery workforce.

papers.abstract_full: Background  The Schizophrenia Exome Meta-Analysis (SCHEMA) Consortium has recently identified 40 genes at a false discovery rate Methods  We screened 9,821 sequenced participants with psychotic disorders who passed genomic quality control from the SUPER-Finland psychosis study for ultra-rare variants predicted to be damaging in these 40 SZ-associated genes, identifying 163 variant carriers. To assess the impact of these variants on clinical course and functioning across psychotic disorders, we used five decades of nationwide, full-coverage health register data together with interview, questionnaire, and cognitive assessments collected at study enrollment. We compared the clinical trajectories and functional outcomes of these variant carriers with those of non-carriers, including comparisons across different strata of the schizophrenia polygenic risk score (SZ-PGS) and with participants harboring deleterious variants in other genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Results  Overall, the variant carriers had a similar distribution of major psychotic disorder diagnoses to that of non-carriers. Despite this diagnostic similarity, variant carriers had earlier hospital admissions than non-carriers for both psychiatric (HR=2.30 [1.48-3.57], p=2.05e-04) and non-psychiatric diagnoses (HR=1.40 [1.10-1.79], p=6.88e-03), indicating increased medical needs early in life. They also showed greater exposure to childhood adversity, lower attainment of adult social milestones, and poorer neuropsychological test performance at study inclusion. Across longitudinal measures, variant carriers showed less favorable clinical and functional trajectories than non-carriers and clustered more closely with individuals with high SZ-PGS (≥90th percentile). Consistent with a liability-threshold model, the variant carriers had lower SZ-PGS than non-carriers among participants with a diagnosis of SZ (β = -0.40, p = 5.32e-05) but higher SZ-PGS than population controls (β = 0.55, p = 9.36e-08), suggesting that the variant carriers developed psychosis at lower levels of common-variant liability. Gene-level analyses identified associations of variants in  AKAP11 ,  SETD1A , and  XPO7 with lower SZ-PGS and/or poorer neuropsychological test performance, while carriers of damaging variants in SZ-risk genes also associated with bipolar disorder showed high cumulative burdens of affective disorder diagnoses.  Conclusion  The disease trajectories of carriers of ultra-rare damaging variants in SZ-risk genes broadly overlapped with those of non-carriers, but carriers showed several differences: greater childhood adversity, earlier hospitalizations, and poorer neuropsychological test performance. These carrier-associated differences were detectable across psychotic disorder diagnoses and suggest a broader phenotypic impact of rare SZ-risk variants than is captured by SZ diagnosis alone, with potential clinical relevance for future risk stratification and genetic counseling.
