papers.abstract_full: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, characterized by progressive cognitive decline and neurodegeneration. Although amyloid-β plaques and hyperphosphorylated tau are major pathological hallmarks, increasing evidence highlights persistent neuroinflammation as a critical contributor to disease progression. Activated microglia and astrocytes, inflammatory cytokines, inflammasome activation, and dysregulated immune responses promote neuronal damage and synaptic dysfunction. Similar inflammatory mechanisms are observed in neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis (MS) and brain tumors, suggesting shared molecular pathways linking neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, and tumor-associated immune responses. Proteomics, transcriptomics, and multi-omics approaches provide powerful strategies to characterize disease-associated molecular signatures, signaling pathways, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. This review summarizes key neuroinflammatory mechanisms in AD, including NF-κB, NLRP3, PI3K/Akt, MAPK, cGAS-STING, mitochondrial, lysosomal, calcium, insulin, and blood-brain barrier pathways. Recent advances in proteomic and transcriptomic profiling and their integration with genomic, epigenomic, and metabolomic data are discussed for understanding disease heterogeneity and identifying clinically relevant biomarkers. Current and emerging therapeutic strategies, including anti-Aβ antibodies, anti-inflammatory agents, selective inhibitors, dual-target compounds, PROTACs, and protein-protein interaction modulators, are also evaluated. Finally, multi-omics-based precision medicine and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis may facilitate biomarker-guided patient stratification and development of effective disease-modifying therapies.

papers.abstract_full: We developed a novel scalable framework that tracks the evolution of research topics across many journals and applied it to biomedical informatics, a field central to digital medicine, contributing methods for semantic harmonization across heterogeneous publication metadata. We analyzed 78,073 articles from 29 PubMed-indexed journals (2011-2025) carrying 95,872 distinct keywords: 75% author-supplied via PubMed or publishers, 24% substituted MeSH descriptors, 1% generated from abstracts. Three overlapping waves emerged: genomics and foundational informatics, machine learning, and generative AI. Attention shifted in 34 of 70 methodology and 22 of 86 health topics; rises persisted on author-supplied keywords alone, whereas most declines disappeared, implying that changes in keyword source, not waning attention, explain most apparent declines. Digital health technologies was the connective topic, clinical and computational collaboration grew, and the Journal of Biomedical Informatics bridged the journal communities. The framework can be applied to other biomedical research fields to identify emerging research priorities.

papers.abstract_full: DNA encodes the cell's phenotype, but the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently in every cell type, developmental stage, and activity state. Existing deep-learning models solve only half of this puzzle: sequence-to-function models read DNA but treat cell state as a fixed label, while single-cell foundation models represent cell state but not sequence. We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA. Trained on 10.7 million cells from 33 datasets across six mammals, Bolero matched or exceeded specialised models and resolved regulatory differences between closely related cell states, including cortical regional and developmental gradients. Extrapolating cell-state embeddings extended Bolero's predictions to cell states that are absent from training. Cell-state conditioning facilitated tracing of the effects of non-coding variants to the cell types in which they act. Using an AP-1 activity score as a further continuous conditioning axis, Bolero predicted activity-regulated chromatin changes without requiring actual stimulation data. Across human cell types, we reconstructed the cooperative grammar of motif identity and spacing underlying predicted AP-1 responses. Bolero further predicted cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility and AP-1 responses in species excluded from training, extending comparative genomics from sequence conservation to predicted functional conservation. Across 84 mammals, we found that predicted AP-1 responses were less conserved than chromatin accessibility at cis-regulatory elements, driven by the human-specific sequence variants on AP-1 and cooperating motifs. By combining reference genomes with reference cell atlases, Bolero allowed genome sequences, either native or mutated, to be queried across cell states, perturbations, and different species for their chromatin and expression signatures.

papers.title: scRM: A single-cell foundation model trained on scRNA-seq reads
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models currently learn from gene count matrices, which are discretized, species-specific summaries that discard the RNA sequence, splice-site usage, 3′ UTR isoform identity and the mutational information present in the underlying sequencing reads. Here we introduce single-cell raw data pretraining, a framework that trains foundation models directly on sequencing reads, requiring no read alignment or count matrix, allowing any trained model to be applicable to arbitrary spe…
papers.abstract_full: Single-cell foundation models currently learn from gene count matrices, which are discretized, species-specific summaries that discard the RNA sequence, splice-site usage, 3′ UTR isoform identity and the mutational information present in the underlying sequencing reads. Here we introduce single-cell raw data pretraining, a framework that trains foundation models directly on sequencing reads, requiring no read alignment or count matrix, allowing any trained model to be applicable to arbitrary species. Our first model in this framework, the single-cell read model scRM, pairs two transformer encoders with a hierarchy of attention pools and contains 1.2 million parameters. We trained it as a JEPA on 3,000 mouse neuron cells on a single H100 in one hour, and benchmarked it zero-shot against leading single-cell foundation models with orders of magnitude more parameters and training cells. Our results show that our lightweight model reaches the performance of existing models on all tasks, and exceeds every one of them on perturbation detection tasks whose detection requires sequence-level detail. To our knowledge, scRM is the first single-cell foundation model trained on sequencing reads, demonstrating that raw data pretraining is not only feasible but competitive at a fraction of the computational cost. We anticipate that scaling this framework and exploring alternative architectures will unlock biological information inaccessible to count models and extend the dataset-specific pretraining it already makes possible. The source code is available at  https://github.com/altos-labs/scRM .

Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their qu…
papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in computational biology, yet their reliability in executing complex scientific workflows remains poorly characterized. Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their quantitative outputs varied substantially: execution times spanned a 31fold range (61 − 1,920 s), while cross-model coefficients of variation reached 142.1%. Notably, four of five agents (80%) exhibited “silent methodological failures,” generating computationally valid, error-free code that produced biologically implausible results. Among the evaluated agents, GLM 5.1 showed the most balanced performance across computational efficiency and biological plausibility. These findings demonstrate that successful code execution alone does not ensure scientific validity and highlight cross-model concordance and biological validation as important quality-control strategies for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted computational biology workflows.

papers.abstract_full: SUMMARY  Treatment options are limited for the priority fungal pathogen  Cryptococcus neoformans . We describe CRISPR-insert, a scalable gene inactivation method for global interrogation of drug targets. Genome-wide screens using this methodology combined with machine learning predict 1,297 essential genes under liberal criteria. Unexpectedly absent from this list is  FKS1 , encoding the target of echinocandin drugs to which  C. neoformans is resistant. Contrary to longstanding literature, targeted deletion shows that  FKS1 is not essential. Solid-state NMR reveals that  fks1 Δ mutants lack β-1,3-glucan, arguing against compensation by another synthase. We experimentally test essentiality predictions for genes lacking human orthologs, identifying high-priority drug target candidates. To uncover targets for combination therapies, we establish genome-scale quantitative genetic interaction mapping. We use this method to uncover synthetic lethal dependencies of echinocandin resistance determinants, including the druggable calcineurin and Cdc50-Apt1 pathways. CRISPR-insert illuminates therapeutic vulnerabilities of an invasive fungal pathogen.

papers.abstract_full: Heart failure (HF) is a diverse clinical syndrome resulting from structural or functional cardiac abnormalities, leading to impaired cardiac output and increased filling pressures. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to guide therapy, improve prognosis, and reduce morbidity and mortality. This review outlines a contemporary stepwise diagnostic framework that reflects a real-world approach, integrating clinical evaluation, laboratory testing, imaging, and hemodynamic assessment. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarkers, including B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal proBNP (NT-proBNP), and echocardiography, which remain the backbone of HF diagnosis, while advanced imaging, genetic testing, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing are used to resolve diagnostic uncertainty in select complex cases. Rather than treating HF as a single entity, this review highlights specific etiologies, including ischemic, genetic, inflammatory, infiltrative, endocrine, and arrhythmogenic causes, and their specific diagnostic considerations. Novel biomarkers, implanted pressure monitoring, and artificial intelligence are examples of emerging techniques that are beginning to complement traditional testing and offer opportunities for early detection, individualized treatment, and preventive measures. By combining traditional and innovative diagnostic tools, clinicians can identify HF promptly, tailor therapy to underlying causes, and ultimately improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

papers.abstract_full: UNLABELLED: China's oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value-driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

papers.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for inducing durable and tumour-specific immune responses; however, their clinical efficacy remains limited by poor antigen immunogenicity, inefficient delivery, tumor heterogeneity, and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). papers.abstract_full: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for inducing durable and tumour-specific immune responses; however, their clinical efficacy remains limited by poor antigen immunogenicity, inefficient delivery, tumor heterogeneity, and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in nanotechnology have expanded opportunities for the rational engineering of multifunctional nanoparticle (NP) platforms that can protect therapeutic cargo, enhance antigen presentation and lymphatic transport, co-deliver immunostimulatory adjuvants, and potentially improve immune modulation while reducing systemic exposure. This narrative review provides an overview of next-generation cancer nanovaccines, including lipid-, polymer-, peptide-, inorganic-, biomimetic-, theranostic, in situ-, and stimuli-responsive platforms, with emphasis on their physicochemical design principles, mechanisms of immune activation, and interactions with the TME. Particular attention is given to strategies targeting tumor -associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and tumor cells to support dendritic-cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell activation, and anti-tumor immunity. Emerging personalized approaches, including neoantigen- and autologous cell-based nanovaccines, mRNA vaccine platforms, and combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors, are also discussed. In addition, we examine the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational immunology in neoantigen prioritization, nanoparticle formulation optimization, immunogenicity prediction, and patient-specific vaccine design. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, most cancer nanovaccine platforms remain at the preclinical or early clinical stage, and translation is limited by tumor heterogeneity, variable immune responses, long-term safety and biodistribution concerns, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory requirements. Overall, the integration of nanotechnology, immunology, precision medicine, and AI offers considerable potential to advance personalized cancer vaccination, but broader clinical validation and standardized manufacturing and evaluation frameworks are required before these platforms can achieve routine clinical application.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Electronic health record (EHR)-related administrative burden remains a frequently cited contributor to clinician burnout in the United States. Although digital systems were implemented to improve quality, safety, and care coordination, expanded documentation requirements, inbox messaging, and regulatory reporting have increased clerical workload. Traditional interruptive clinical decision support tools may further increase cognitive demands through alert fatigue and workflow disruption. Health systems have increasingly adopted predictive analytics and workflow-integrated automation, including ambient artificial intelligence (AI) documentation, inbox prioritization, and audit log-based workflow monitoring. However, their effects on operational efficiency and clinician well-being remain uncertain. This review examined clinician-facing interventions in US clinical settings and their impact on documentation workload, operational efficiency, and burnout-related outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review guided by Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase. The search included English-language studies published between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2025, with an updated search capturing eligible early online publications through 2026. Eligible studies evaluated clinician-facing predictive analytics or workflow automation in US clinical settings and reported measurable outcomes, including documentation time, after-hours EHR use, alert burden, cognitive task load, productivity, or validated burnout measures. Findings were synthesized narratively because interventions and outcome measures varied. RESULTS: Of 520 records identified, 173 unique records were screened; 24 (13.9%) underwent full-text review, and 7 of 24 (29.2%) met inclusion criteria. Ambient AI documentation platforms were associated with approximately 10%-30% reductions in documentation time, although findings on after-hours EHR activity varied. Several multisite implementations reported improvements in validated burnout measures and cognitive task load. AI-driven inbox prioritization reduced message review time, while audit log-based clinical decision support monitoring identified changes in EHR activity patterns following intervention. Evidence quality varied, and follow-up periods were generally short. CONCLUSIONS: Workflow-integrated predictive analytics and automation interventions were associated with measurable improvements in documentation workload and selected burnout indicators in US clinical settings. However, evidence remains mixed and largely observational. Rigorous, multisite, longitudinal evaluations using standardized workload and burnout metrics are needed to determine sustainability and generalizability.

We begin by comparing conventional microscopy with digital pathology and outlining the major components of the digital pathology workflow. We then explore whole-slide imaging, its imaging modalities, scanner technologies, image storage, and image management systems. We then examine the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital pathology, discussing current AI applications and the spectrum of computational approaches, from conventional feature-engineering methods to deep learning and multimodal models. Finally, we review the clinical applications of digital pathology, summarize its implementation across US medical centers, and discuss the technical, regulatory, and operational challenges that must be addressed for broader clinical adoption.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is molecularly heterogeneous, and computationally nominated biomarkers often lack sufficient functional validation. CALB1 is a calcium-binding protein, but its clinical relevance, cellular source, and signaling role in NSCLC remain unclear. This study aimed to identify subtype-associated regulators in NSCLC through a machine-learning-assisted multi-omics framework and to characterize the functional and signaling relevance of CALB1 in malignant progression. METHODS: NSCLC transcriptomic cohorts were used to define metabolic-epigenetic remodeling (MER) subtypes. Machine-learning-assisted Cox modeling was then applied to identify subtype-associated prognostic regulators. CALB1 was selected for further validation using public cohorts, in-house NSCLC specimens, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), western blotting, immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling, and functional assays. CALB1 was silenced in A549 and PC9 cells to assess its effects on PI3K/AKT activation, proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated phenotypes. Alpelisib was used as a PI3Kα inhibitor to examine the pathway-level involvement of PI3K/AKT signaling in CALB1-associated phenotypes. In vivo relevance and alpelisib responsiveness were further evaluated using a four-group subcutaneous A549 xenograft model comprising sh-Control + vehicle, sh-CALB1 + vehicle, sh-Control + alpelisib, and sh-CALB1 + alpelisib groups. RESULTS: Three MER subtypes were identified, with MER2 showing the poorest prognosis and distinct immune-metabolic features. CALB1 was retained in the prognostic model and positively correlated with model-derived risk scores. CALB1 was upregulated in NSCLC tissues, associated with advanced clinicopathological features and unfavorable prognosis, and mainly enriched in malignant epithelial cells. CALB1-high tumors showed enrichment of proliferative, metabolic, DNA repair, and PI3K/AKT-related programs. CALB1 knockdown induced coordinated proteomic and phosphoproteomic changes involving proliferation, migration, extracellular matrix organization, secretory trafficking, and PI3K/AKT signaling. Functionally, CALB1 silencing reduced p-PI3K and p-AKT levels and suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-associated phenotypes. PI3Kα inhibition with alpelisib attenuated CALB1 overexpression-associated malignant phenotypes in vitro. In vivo, stable CALB1 knockdown suppressed xenograft growth and enhanced the antitumor response to alpelisib, with the sh-CALB1 + alpelisib group showing the greatest reductions in tumor volume and tumor weight. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies CALB1 as a subtype-associated regulator in NSCLC through a machine-learning-assisted multi-omics framework. CALB1 may promote malignant progression partly through PI3K/AKT-related signaling. Stable CALB1 knockdown increased the in vivo antitumor response to alpelisib, supporting CALB1 as a potential modulator of PI3Kα inhibitor sensitivity.

CALB1 was retained in the prognostic model and positively correlated with model-derived risk scores.

papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. papers.abstract_full: Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. Yet most existing methods for immunotherapy response prediction rely on independent signatures or cell types and fail to model the structured and directional signaling network within the TME. To address this gap, we introduce EcoNet, a computational framework that first models ecosystems consisting of co-occurring cell states, then constructs intercellular and intracellular signaling networks based on the ecosystems, and applies a graph attention network to derive embeddings from the signaling network for immunotherapy response prediction. Pretrained on 2,532 pan-cancer immunotherapy samples across multiple cohorts, EcoNet outperformed existing prediction methods by 7.5-19.9% and marker-based signatures by 4.4-21.2% in AUC, and its high-attention genes were enriched among those required for T-cell-mediated tumor killing in an independent CRISPR screen; applied to ccRCC with disease-specific fine-tuning, it stratified an independent ccRCC cohort by clinical outcome ( P =0.024). Biologically, high-attention genes capture an interferon-responsive program that enhances antigen presentation and immune infiltration. To validate these findings, we curated a ccRCC clinical cohort profiled with CosMx single-cell spatial transcriptomics (46 samples, ~450,000 cells) and found the response-associated TME configuration identified by EcoNet localized to immune-enriched niches, supporting the response stratification. These results establish EcoNet as a generalizable framework for TME-informed therapeutic response prediction, readily extensible to other cancer types and therapeutic contexts.

papers.abstract_full: Radiation dose in medical imaging has been quantified through measurable metrics such as computed tomography dose index volume (CTDIvol), dose length product (DLP), kerma area product, kerma at reference point etc. They are benchmarked through diagnostic reference levels (DRLs); and communicated in terms of effective dose and population-based risk estimates. None of these tools was designed to describe the dose, the reference standard, or the risk applicable to the individual patient. In every other domain of medicine where a potentially harmful agent accompanies a beneficial clinical intervention, from contrast nephrotoxicity in CT imaging to anesthetic risk in surgery, the field has moved beyond population metrics to individualized measurement and individual clinical decision-making. Radiation protection in medical imaging has not yet made this transition. This paper resolves several open questions on cumulative dose that have long been used to justify inaction. It argues that the transition is now technically achievable, that the barriers to it are primarily architectural, regulatory, and cultural rather than physical or computational, and that artificial intelligence and emerging imaging technologies provide the enabling infrastructure to complete it. We describe the three-tier structure of barriers to individual dose tracking: technical, institutional and regulatory, and cultural; and propose the elements of a system that would place the individual patient's cumulative radiation dose record where it belongs: in their medical record, alongside their medication list, visible at the point of every subsequent clinical imaging decision.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME). Apoptotic protease-activating factor 1 (APAF1) is a core component of mitochondrial apoptosis; however, its association with immune characteristics, spatial heterogeneity and compound discovery in GC remains poorly defined. METHODS: The bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning-based modeling, immune deconvolution and spatial niche analysis were integrated to characterize APAF1-associated features in GC. Machine learning-guided computational screening combining molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations was used to prioritize morellic acid (MA). The biological effects of MA and the involvement of APAF1-associated signaling were evaluated through in vitro and in vivo assays using APAF1-targeting siRNA and shRNA, respectively. RESULTS: APAF1 expression was increased in GC, particularly in early-stage tumors and was independently associated with improved overall survival after multivariable adjustment (HR = 0.681, 95% CI: 0.494-0.940, P = 0.0196). However, its standalone prognostic discrimination was limited, with time-dependent ROC analyses showing poor predictive performance. Tumor-versus-normal ROC analysis demonstrated differential expression between GC and normal tissues (AUC = 0.875, 95% CI: 0.823-0.918). Single-cell and spatial analyses revealed that APAF1 expression was associated with distinct immune-cell patterns and tumor spatial niches. Machine learning-guided computational screening prioritized MA as a candidate compound. MA inhibited GC cell proliferation and migration (IC50: 1.807 ± 0.16 to 6.216 ± 0.23 μM) and suppressed tumor growth in vivo, achieving tumor inhibition rates of 79.32 ± 7.69%, 92.37 ± 4.21%, and 92.19 ± 2.99% at low, medium and high doses, respectively. APAF1 silencing attenuated MA-associated changes in cleaved Caspase-3 activation and GSDME-NT accumulation, suggesting the involvement of APAF1-associated cell-death signaling. CONCLUSION: APAF1 is associated with distinct tumor microenvironment characteristics and clinical features in GC, supporting its potential relevance to tumor biology beyond its canonical role in mitochondrial apoptosis. The novelty of this study lies in extending the investigation of APAF1 beyond its canonical apoptotic function by integrating machine learning with multimodal transcriptomic and spatial analyses to characterize APAF1-associated TME features and computationally prioritize MA. All the findings provide a cross-scale framework linking APAF1-associated tumor biology with candidate compound screening and MA-related cell-death responses in GC.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Liver metastasis (LM) is a major determinant of poor prognosis in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), yet reliable biomarkers for identifying patients at high metastatic risk remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a tumor cell origin-based metastasis risk score (TCOMRS) for characterizing LM-associated transcriptional features in COAD and to identify key molecular regulators involved in liver metastatic progression. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiles from primary tumors and LM were integrated to identify distinct malignant-cell subpopulations and delineate their cellular origins. TCOMRS was constructed based on a one-class logistic regression (OCLR) algorithm trained with 4,512 malignant cells derived from LM, enabling assessment of the similarity between primary tumor cells and LM-associated malignant phenotypes. The clinical relevance of TCOMRS was validated across multiple independent cohorts, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-COAD, GSE39582, GSE38832, and GSE161158. RESULTS: Elevated TCOMRS was consistently associated with unfavorable overall survival, increased tumor stemness, and the presence of LM. Moreover, patients with low TCOMRS demonstrated improved responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade therapy, suggesting potential utility in therapeutic decision-making. Mechanistically, fatty acid-binding protein 1 (FABP1) was identified as a key driver of LM, facilitating epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastatic colonization. FABP1 expression correlated strongly with TCOMRS and metastatic propensity. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish TCOMRS as a robust biomarker for risk stratification and FABP1 as a promising therapeutic target, offering valuable insights for personalized treatment strategies in COAD.

papers.abstract_full: Evidence-based medicine represents the systematic approach through which physicians today use the best available scientific evidence from clinical research to guide their clinical decision-making process. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), with its diverse models and potential applications in medicine, is leading to a new form of research driven by 'big data' and heterogeneous datasets, extending beyond conventional statistical analysis and thereby making AI literacy an increasingly essential competence for clinicians. Artificial intelligence applications in cardiology have shown potential to support disease diagnosis, risk prediction, workflow efficiency, and therapeutic decision-making. However, despite these opportunities, AI may also represent a technological barrier for many physicians, due to its mathematical foundations and the speed at which models evolve. A solid understanding of AI concepts is therefore necessary for cardiologists to critically interpret results and engage with this new research landscape. This scientific statement explores AI in cardiology from an educational perspective, outlining the key knowledge required to build adequate AI literacy. The goal is to enable cardiologists not only to avoid reliance on external experts for methodological decisions, but also to collaborate with greater insight and informed judgment.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS. METHODS: GEO expression profiles were analyzed via differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment analyses. A Random Forest model evaluated key genes, validating their expression and diagnostic performance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) further assessed their expression patterns, and a Transcription Factor (TF)-mRNA-miRNA regulatory network. RESULTS: Fifteen overlapping genes were identified, from which six candidates were screened through a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network and validated in vitro. The application of a Random Forest model identified two key hub genes, CCL5 and IL1B, which were significantly upregulated. Their diagnostic Area Under the Curve (AUC) was >0.7 when assessed separately and increased to >0.85 in a combined model. Three shared TFs (NFKBIA, NFKB1, RELA) of the Nuclear Factor-kappa B (NF-κB) pathway were identified, highlighting its central role in disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: CCL5 and IL1B are key genes potentially regulating EndMT-mediated AS via inflammatory pathways including Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like (NOD-like) receptor, Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF), and NF-κB signaling, offering promising diagnostic and therapeutic targets for AS.

Concurrently, patients increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) large language model (LLM) chatbots to obtain health information. We evaluated the completeness and guideline concordance of AI-generated responses to patient-style questions about regenerative ED therapies, and their consistency across repeated queries. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional evaluation of four general-purpose LLM platforms: ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5, Claude 3.7, and Copilot. Six patient-style prompts addressing general inquiry, evidence appraisal, safety, and treatment-seeking behavior were submitted for each therapy (SCT, LiSWT, PRP) in two independent sessions on separate days, yielding 144 responses. The primary outcome was the presence of nine prespecified counseling elements using a binary checklist. The secondary outcome was concordance with the Sexual Medicine Society of North America (SMSNA) position statement, assessed across efficacy framing, recommendation against routine use, and regulatory-status accuracy. Within-platform consistency across two sessions was assessed using Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Most responses identified investigational or non-FDA-approved status (80.6%), recommended physician consultation (76.4%), and acknowledged limitations in current research (75%). References to society guidelines (14.6%), safety profiles (38.9%), alternative therapies (23.6%), and cost (31.9%) were uncommon. Peer-reviewed citations were present in fewer than half of responses (47.9%), despite frequent references to "research". Among the 130 responses that characterized efficacy, only 36% conveyed the guideline-concordant position that clinical efficacy has not been established for regenerative therapies. The majority of responses instead framed efficacy optimistically despite the lack of robust efficacy evidence. An explicit recommendation against routine clinical use appeared in only 18.8% of responses. Within-platform consistency was substantial for Copilot, Claude, and Gemini (κ=0.61-0.67) and moderate for ChatGPT (κ=0.54). CONCLUSIONS: General-purpose AI chatbots provide incomplete counseling regarding regenerative ED therapies and inconsistently reflect the core elements of the SMSNA position statement. Chatbot responses specifically contain gaps in disclosing safety profiles, approved alternatives, and cost. Deliberate integration of evidence-based guidance into consumer-facing LLMs is needed to prevent AI-driven misconceptions. Clinicians should assess AI use and address AI-derived expectations during clinical encounters.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is biologically heterogeneous, and epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity contributes to invasion and treatment resistance. We aimed to develop a distal-less homeobox 4 (DLX4)-anchored pathomics model for overall survival (OS) and to relate routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) morphology to malignant epithelial and spatial states. METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis used public The Cancer Genome Atlas-Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-KIRC) and Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) ccRCC data accessed and frozen in June 2026. Patients with ccRCC, positive OS time, known vital status, and matched whole-slide-image pathomics features were eligible. TCGA was used for model fitting (506 patients; 167 deaths). CPTAC (94 patients; 20 deaths) contributed to cross-cohort feature confirmation and algorithm ranking and therefore was not an untouched external-validation cohort. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes were screened using database of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (dbEMT) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox regression (LASSO-Cox). Direction-consistent DLX4-associated features were filtered in TCGA and evaluated in a 101-style survival machine-learning library. The final eight-component partial least squares Cox (plsRcox) model used 705 standardized predictors. Bulk, single-cell, copy-number, trajectory, and spatial analyses were used for biological interpretation. RESULTS: LASSO-Cox retained 19 EMT genes, and DLX4 was prioritized as an adverse-prognosis anchor. Of 1,192 direction-consistent DLX4-pathomics features, 705 passed TCGA univariable Cox filtering. Of 117 prespecified parameterized jobs, 63 generated finite paired TCGA-CPTAC risk scores and were evaluable. The selected plsRcox model yielded an apparent TCGA C-index of 0.877 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.853-0.900] and a CPTAC cross-cohort C-index of 0.775 (95% CI: 0.617-0.915). The fixed TCGA median cutoff separated CPTAC low-risk (44 patients; 4 deaths) and high-risk (50 patients; 16 deaths) groups (log-rank P=0.008). Adding the pathomics score to age, stage, and grade increased the C-index in TCGA by 0.121 (95% CI: 0.089-0.158), but this increment was not reproduced in CPTAC (-0.019; 95% CI: -0.184 to 0.118). CONCLUSIONS: The DLX4-associated pathomics score was associated with OS and with malignant epithelial and spatial remodeling in ccRCC. Because CPTAC influenced feature confirmation and algorithm ranking, its performance is a cross-cohort evaluation rather than unbiased external validation. The model and its incremental clinical value require locked, independent multicenter evaluation before clinical use.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To define clinically relevant glioma ecosystem states (recurrent spatial configurations of malignant programs and microenvironmental niches) and identify immune-niche-dependent therapeutic vulnerabilities using single-nucleus, spatial, tissue, and machine-learning analyses. METHODS: Public multi-omics datasets were integrated with institutional single-nucleus RNA sequencing from 12 tumors, spatial transcriptomics from 6 IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, multiplex immunofluorescence in 138 FFPE cases, and glioma-macrophage co-culture assays. RESULTS: Three ecosystem states were identified. The hypoxic myeloid-mesenchymal state showed the highest MES-like, hypoxia, SPP1/APOE myeloid, and temozolomide-resistance scores, the lowest CD8+ T-cell density, and the shortest tumor-myeloid distance. In 96 IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, this state independently predicted shorter progression-free survival (HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.22-3.92) and overall survival (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.12-3.81) after adjustment for major clinical and molecular covariates. Defactinib plus temozolomide reduced viability, colony formation, and migration by 56.0%, 61.3%, and 57.8%, respectively, under macrophage-conditioned culture. CONCLUSION: Spatially organized tumor-immune ecosystems provide prognostic information and highlight potentially actionable SPP1-CD44/FAK-SRC signaling in glioblastoma as a candidate target for individualized therapeutic stratification approaches.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study. METHODS: Genes with differential expression (DEGs) were pinpointed from the GSE89632 dataset, which includes 39 MASH samples compared with 24 controls. Candidate genes were identified using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) and gene sets related to neuroinflammation. A diagnostic model was constructed using 81 machine learning algorithm combinations (filtered from an initial set of 113 by excluding models with fewer than 2 features) within the training set, and its performance was subsequently evaluated in GSE126848 (31 MASH vs. 26 controls) as an evaluation set. Because the evaluation set contributed to model selection, it does not represent a fully independent validation cohort. Regulatory network construction, drug prediction, and molecular docking were used for further analysis of key genes. RESULTS: A total of 90 disease-associated neuroinflammation-related candidate genes were identified. Five candidate key genes (IRS1, HBEGF, MYC, CD274, and HMOX1) were screened, and a diagnostic model was constructed. The model achieved an AUC of 0.978 in the training set and 0.823 in the evaluation set; however, because the evaluation set contributed to model selection in the original analysis, the 0.823 estimate should be interpreted with caution. These findings are exploratory and require experimental validation. CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory study identified five neuroinflammation-related candidate genes that may serve as candidate biomarkers for MASH. These findings provide candidate molecular links and potential therapeutic hypotheses, but require experimental validation and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than clinically actionable.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention. METHODS: We integrated network toxicology, an ensemble of 112 machine-learning classifiers and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with six GEO cohorts to nominate fibrotic-lung genes, which were intersected with predicted MTX targets to prioritize candidates relevant to MTX-PF. Lead candidates were validated by molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-PBSA binding free energy calculation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). In vivo MTX-induced mouse models and in vitro BEAS-2B assays, including the Transwell migration/invasion, EdU proliferation, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, CA4 and TLR4 overexpression, and a CA4/TLR4 co-overexpression rescue experiment, were performed to assess the regulatory role of the top-ranked gene. RESULTS: Carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) ranked first by SHAP importance (0.120) and diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.879); the Ridge model discriminated training and validation cohorts (AUC = 0.930, 0.897 and 0.864). MTX bound stably to CA4 in silico (Vina -7.078 kcal/mol; MM-PBSA ΔGbind -76.5 kJ/mol), and SPR detected concentration-dependent binding to recombinant CA4 (KD = 6.25 μM), identifying CA4 as a candidate direct binding partner. In MTX-treated mice, CA4 was downregulated while TLR4, collagen deposition and serum TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IFN-α and IFN-β were elevated. In BEAS-2B cells, CA4 overexpression suppressed migration, invasion and proliferation, reversed MTX-induced upregulation of TLR4, NF-κB, IRF3, VIM, FN1 and COL1A1, and restored E-cadherin. Forced TLR4 overexpression reversed the protective effect of CA4 and re-established the inflammatory and mesenchymal phenotype. CONCLUSION: In MTX-PF, MTX directly binds CA4 in vitro. CA4 loss accompanies coordinate upregulation of the TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 axis and an EMT program coupling epithelial injury to fibrogenesis, and CA4 restoration reverses this program in epithelial cells. Although TLR4 gain-of-function abrogated CA4-mediated suppression, its causal necessity remains untested. Given that TLR4 signaling is context-dependent and can facilitate inflammation resolution in some fibrosis models, therapeutic blockade requires careful attention to cell type and timing. CA4 thus represents a candidate molecular correlate and experimental target, pending clinical and in vivo validation.

papers.abstract_full: Motivation  Single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) technologies enable the study of three-dimensional (3D) genome organization at individual-cell resolution. Many computational methods have been developed to infer hierarchical structures from scHi-C data. However, annotating chromatin subcompartments from sparse scHi-C data remains a challenge. The recently developed scGHOST provides a framework for single-cell subcompartment annotation, but relies on a deep learning-based architecture, a multi-step upstream pipeline involving cell embedding and matrix imputation, and cross-cell information sharing. These features complicate algorithmic interpretation and make the annotation of an individual cell dependent on information from other cells in the dataset. Hence, methods are needed that annotate subcompartments directly from an individual cell’s own contact matrix, without complex upstream processing or cross-cell information sharing. Results  We developed scSTEC, a computational framework that annotates subcompartments directly from an individual scHi-C matrix without data imputation, complex upstream processing, or cross-cell data sharing. We show that the estimated inter-chromosomal matrix constructed by scGHOST is intrinsically of rank 2, revealing that the geometry relevant to clustering can be represented in two dimensions. Leveraging this low-dimensional structure, scSTEC performs direct subcompartment annotation through 2D genomic embedding and chromosome-wise consensus. Across bulk Hi-C, downsampled simulations, and real scHi-C datasets (four human cell lines, adult mouse cortex, developing mouse embryos, and developing olfactory sensory neurons), scSTEC achieves subcompartment annotations comparable to scGHOST despite operating on each cell independently, while providing greater algorithmic interpretability. Furthermore, subcompartments identified by scSTEC effectively resolve cell types, capture developmental dynamics, and show consistent associations with gene expression and epigenetic profiles. Availability  scSTEC is freely available at  https://github.com/Ge-lab-pku/scSTEC .

papers.abstract_full: Parkinson disease (PD) impairs skilled reaching tasks but less is known about its effects on rhythmic bimanual actions. We used a bimanual hand-over-hand string-pulling task that requires repeated reach, grasp, pull, push and release movements. We predicted that participants with PD would show impairment in making the rotary skilled hand movement of retrieving the string, analogous to impairments observed in single handed target reaching. Nine participants with PD (mean UPDRS-III: 24.6), 16 older adults, and 10 young adults successfully performed a real string-pulling task and then pantomimed the action. Video analyses combined optical-flow estimation of whole-body movement speed, markerless 2D pose estimation of upper-limb kinematics, and expert frame-by-frame scoring of hand and finger shaping. Machine-learning classification then identified the discriminative information carried by these multilevel movement components. Participants with PD showed lower movement speed, a smaller hand workspace, and reduced hand and finger shaping, with older adults showing intermediate values. All participants grasped the real string with a power grip, but participants with PD showed reduced rotary movements of the arm and the wrists and absent of arpeggio-like sequential finger movement during grasp and release. During pantomime, participants with PD moved faster and made larger hand movements, while grasp-related hand opening and finger sequencing was reduced or absent. The findings suggest that PD is expressed across this multicomponent movement manifold, and that the movement organization changes with task demands: real string pulling requires formation and release of a power grip, whereas pantomime does not place demands on grasping ability. New & Noteworthy  Parkinson disease affects multiple movement components, yet their organization during continuous action remains less studied. Using bimanual string pulling, we identified alterations particularly evident in hand opening and finger sequencing despite successful task completion. Older adults showed intermediate values on several measures, while pantomime-related changes in these measures differed across groups. These findings suggest that motor impairment in Parkinson disease includes task-dependent changes in movement organization that successful performance alone can conceal.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 359 records identified, 124 studies and documents met the inclusion criteria: 40 empirical studies, 43 conceptual analyses or commentaries, 20 policy and guidance documents, 17 reviews and 4 methodological frameworks; 83% were published from 2023 onwards. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain accountable. Disclosure thresholds, AI in peer review, AI-generated images, AI-text detectors and the regulatory treatment of research remain contested. Challenges fall into three clusters: algorithmic bias; data governance, privacy and consent; and transparency, reproducibility and integrity, where empirical studies document fabricated references, unreliable and biased detectors, and rapidly rising, mostly undisclosed AI use. Emerging responses include lifecycle-based guidance, structured documentation, tailored ethics review and interdisciplinary oversight. We propose an integrated framework linking five principles to five research stages and an agenda emphasizing context-sensitive ethics, public participation and international coordination.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may help students produce higher-quality work; however, its effects on their future ability to work independently remain unclear. This integrative review examines this distinction by analysing research on feedback, metacognitive monitoring, cognitive offloading, and reconstructive learning activities. Targeted web searches and primary-source tracing informed a focused synthesis of adult learning studies and relevant foundational research. Three features may help explain variation in findings across studies: the information feedback conveys, the reasoning learners are expected to undertake and demonstrate, and the conditions under which learning is assessed. The proposed framework distinguishes between a regulatory pathway, in which feedback informs judgments and learning choices, and a practice pathway, in which reconstruction prompts relevant reasoning. This distinction helps explain why learners may become better calibrated without learning more, or learn more without becoming better calibrated. Feedback is expected to enhance the benefits of reconstruction when it improves engagement or reasoning quality, although its incremental benefit may be limited when the activity already provides comparable practice. Four conditional propositions describe these relationships and suggest comparisons that could help distinguish them from the effects of additional instruction, exposure, time, and motivation. The framework provides a foundation for testing when feedback and reconstruction support performance in the absence of assistance. The available evidence is not yet sufficient to establish the full causal pathways or lasting changes in capability, underscoring the value of delayed assessments, transfer tasks, and longitudinal research.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Air pollution and thermal stress are experienced together but assessed separately. Here we quantify modelled pollution-related shifts in outdoor thermal comfort across Indian states during 2016–2023, using 423 regulatory monitoring stations and reanalysis-based UTCI. At monthly state scale, pollutant anomalies show no statistically detectable association with UTCI anomalies after accounting for seasonality, consistent with nonlinear machine-learning results. A published index integrating both dimensions fails on transfer to India, producing unphysical comfort gains in clean regions. We therefore recalibrate it with Indian regulatory anchors. The recalibrated index estimates winter and post-monsoon comfort-index shifts concentrated across the Indo-Gangetic Plain, reaching 4°C-equivalent in Delhi. A population-weighted dual-exposure classification shows 2.98 billion person-months of model-defined compound exposure each year, two-thirds of India’s thermal-stress burden. This burden is invisible to thermal indices, and to the separate frameworks that currently govern heat and air quality.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. Conventional reference techniques such as gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and standardized wet-chemistry assays remain essential for confirmatory analysis, yet their cost, infrastructure needs, and sample-processing demands limit continuous use at farms, mills, warehouses, and retail inspection points. Here we present a full research framework for a portable spectrophotometric olive oil quality analysis system that integrates ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, near-infrared spectroscopy, chemometric calibration, edge-machine-learning classification, and oxidative stress-state modeling. The system is designed to quantify quality indicators such as free acidity, peroxide value, conjugated diene/triene absorbance, phenolic depletion, pigment degradation, and adulteration-associated spectral deviation without relying on destructive laboratory workflows. The research develops the platform as an analytical chemistry and embedded diagnostic system rather than as a simple consumer sensor. The designed instrument combines controlled optical illumination, wavelength-resolved detection, temperature-compensated sample handling, onboard preprocessing, encrypted data storage, and cloud-supported model governance. The biochemical model links spectral behavior to triglyceride structure, oleic-linoleic acid balance, phenolic antioxidant buffering, radical propagation, hydroperoxide accumulation, aldehyde formation, and the degradation of chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments during light or heat exposure. The computational model couples standard normal variate correction, derivative spectroscopy, principal component analysis, partial least squares regression, support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting, and uncertainty-aware edge inference. A validation strategy is applied using authenticated extra virgin, virgin, refined, and pomace oils; controlled adulteration series with sunflower, soybean, canola, palm, and refined olive oils; and accelerated storage experiments under oxygen, heat, and light stress. Expected outputs include rapid screening of authenticity, estimation of regulatory quality parameters, early detection of oxidative instability, and generation of traceable reports for producers, inspectors, and supply-chain actors. The framework is aligned with international olive oil quality concepts while emphasizing that portable spectroscopy is best positioned as a high-throughput screening and decision-support layer rather than a replacement for legal confirmatory testing.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Big Tech platform self-regulation and national anti-disinformation laws jointly govern political speech in Southeast Asia, a region without a supranational regulatory framework, yet their interaction has not been systematically synthesized. This review examined how they interact in shaping political disinformation and freedom of expression in the region from 2015 to 2025. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched Scopus, ScienceDirect, SAGE Journals, and JSTOR in April–May 2026 for English-language, peer-reviewed studies. Of 3,886 records, 35 studies were included. Quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) 2018, and findings were synthesized thematically around three research questions. A large language model assisted screening, summarization, and initial appraisal, with all outputs checked by the authors. The methods were registered retrospectively on the Open Science Framework (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/BGXHW). Results The studies (2015–2026; 74.3% qualitative) were concentrated in Malaysia and in studies without a single-country focus. Three themes were identified: platform–state interaction (n = 13), regulatory gaps and digital rights safeguards (n = 15), and discursive patterns in platform policies (n = 8). States used legal, technical, and administrative pressure to secure platform compliance, while platforms adapted their moderation largely on pragmatic and commercial grounds. Vaguely defined laws, their misuse, state-linked manipulation, and chilling effects were widely documented, whereas evidence on changes to Terms of Service and on benchmarking against international freedom of expression standards was limited. Platform policy language was strategically ambiguous, and moderation increasingly operated through visibility. Conclusions Ambiguity in both state law and platform policy may function as a feature of governance rather than only as a drafting failure. Improving the governance of online speech in the region is likely to require independent oversight of enforcement, transparency about moderation practice, and co-regulatory arrangements with clearly defined safeguards. Future research should address the underrepresentation of Vietnam, Cambodia, and the Philippines.

In this work, we present a unified resource of 67 human gene-embedding sets derived from protein, DNA and RNA sequences, biomedical text, bulk expression data, single-cell expression models, functional data, biological network…
papers.abstract_full: Gene embeddings are vector representations of gene identity that provide machine-learning models with information from diverse biological sources. However, their use is hindered by a lack of standardization: inconsistent identifiers, formats, and preprocessing conventions. In this work, we present a unified resource of 67 human gene-embedding sets derived from protein, DNA and RNA sequences, biomedical text, bulk expression data, single-cell expression models, functional data, biological networks, knowledge graphs, regulatory genomics and multimodal models, covering up to 20,097 GENCODE-annotated protein-coding genes. The collection includes both published precomputed embeddings and representations generated or extracted from publicly available models and biological data. Each embedding set is organized in a folder containing the embedding matrix, the Ensembl gene identifiers, machine-readable metadata, and processing documentation. We validate the resource by measuring global and local similarity, cross-embedding consensus, and cross-embedding predictability. The collection is designed to allow community-contributed embeddings that meet predefined technical and documentation requirements, enables comparison of gene representations across modalities and provides standardized embeddings for training and downstream applications.

Here, we investigated odor-dependent behavioral organization and VSN sensory representations using three-dimensional behavioral tracking, integrative machine-learning analysis, volumetric calcium imagi…
papers.abstract_full: Natural predator-associated chemosignals elicit diverse defensive behaviors, yet it remains unclear how complex natural cues shape the spatiotemporal organization of risk assessment and activate vomeronasal sensory neurons (VSNs) and downstream circuits in the mammalian accessory olfactory system. Here, we investigated odor-dependent behavioral organization and VSN sensory representations using three-dimensional behavioral tracking, integrative machine-learning analysis, volumetric calcium imaging, and whole-brain FosTRAP2 mapping. We developed a pose-based integrative machine-learning analysis pipeline (PIMAP) to identify behavioral signatures based on posture, spatial exploration, state transitions, and temporal dynamics. We found that common behavioral states were expressed in multiple odor conditions, but their expression rates, spatial positions, and temporal sequencing distinguished responses to snake, tortoise, lizard, and mouse fecal cues. Snake fecal cues elicited sustained direct investigation and distinct patterns of spatial exploration, behavioral transitions, and grooming in both two-chamber and multiple-choice assays. Volumetric calcium imaging in the vomeronasal epithelium revealed distinct patterns of VSN activation by different reptilian cues. Whole-brain microscopy of FosTRAP2 transgenic mice indicated potential differential activity patterns in AOS-associated circuits following snake and tortoise exposure. Furthermore, Trpc2 deletion altered snake-associated behavioral signatures, while odor-discriminative behavioral patterns remained detectable. Together, these findings show that reptilian predator cues activate distinct AOS components and bias exploration patterns towards threat assessment and vigilance.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Multipartite genomes define the genus Vibrio, yet replicon specialisation remains poorly understood, particularly in environmental species. We developed a machine-learning classifier to assign draft contigs to putative replicons with high accuracy, integrating complete and draft genomes in comparative analyses. Independent implementation in Vibrio cholerae yielded similar performance, supporting broader applicability. Analysis of 41 Vibrio coralliilyticus genomes revealed functional specialisation between chromosomes despite similar proportions of core and flexible gene families. Chromosome I was enriched in essential cellular processes, central metabolism, motility and regulation, whereas chromosome II was enriched in environmental sensing, signal transduction, transport and interaction-associated functions. Chromosome I also exhibited greater plasticity, with more extensive homologous recombination and higher densities of mobile genetic elements and defence systems. Two previously undescribed conjugative megaplasmid lineages (254–628 kb) displayed contrasting adaptive repertoires. One was broadly distributed across hosts and geographic regions, encoding a conserved accessory repertoire including a giant multidomain putative effector predicted to mediate host interactions. The other was restricted to Mediterranean coral isolates, with an expanded mobilome and a conserved Sofic-like anti-phage defence system. Together, these findings show that functional specialisation can coexist with similar gene conservation patterns, while chromosomes and megaplasmids make complementary contributions to adaptation and genome evolution.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Genetic conditions are common in congenital heart disease (CHD) and affect care, but are often missed or diagnosed late. We asked whether routine clinical data can shortlist the most likely genetic conditions. METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort of children with CHD and an echocardiogram who had either a confirmed genetic diagnosis or negative cytogenetic testing and CHD gene sequencing. Echocardiogram images and serial medical record data were added as model inputs in the order they become clinically available. Class-balanced logistic regression (LR) and a multimodal deep learning fusion network were fitted to the same inputs at each step. The primary metric was balanced top-3 accuracy (correct diagnosis among the top three, averaged across conditions), with bootstrap intervals. RESULTS: The cohort included 1,720 children (988 with common CHD-associated genetic conditions, 231 rare diagnoses, 501 negative testing). Using only inputs generated at the echocardiogram visit, LR reached a balanced top-3 accuracy 0.758 (chance 0.429). Serial records, radiology notes and ICD-10 codes, raised this to 0.809. Multimodal fusion performed similarly at each stage. With a genetic condition withheld from training, the fusion embedding placed affected children nearest to others sharing a gene group in 0.37 of cases versus 0.10 without the embedding (+0.268 [95% CI +0.242, +0.295]). CONCLUSIONS: Routine clinical data available at first echocardiogram can help identify likely genetic diagnoses, and later coded inputs ceiling. Multimodal fusion added no accuracy over LR, but places children sharing a genetic cause near one another, making nearest-neighbor retrieval informative for undiagnosed children.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS) is a severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of left-sided cardiac structures, requiring staged surgical palliation that establishes the right ventricle as the single ventricle maintaining systemic circulation. After surgery, patients remain highly susceptible to heart failure, possibly due to the increased hemodynamic load imposed on the single surviving ventricle. Because the etiology of HLHS remains poorly understood, elucidating the mechanisms that drive ventricular dysfunction requires model systems that capture both patient-specific genetics and the dynamic mechanical environment of the ventricle. Thus, our objective was to compare how induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from patients with HLHS differ from control in static culture and in response to cyclic stretch. METHODS: Control iPSCs from two unaffected donors and iPSCs from four HLHS patients were differentiated into iPSC-CMs, engineered into aligned tissues, and cultured statically or exposed to cyclic 20% uniaxial stretch at 1 Hz for 48h. Sarcomere organization was quantified in static tissues using images of immunostained α-actinin. Calcium transients at 1 Hz pacing frequency in static and stretched tissues were evaluated using Fluo-4 calcium indicator dye. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to evaluate stretch-induced transcriptomic changes in control and HLHS iPSC-CMs. RESULTS: In static culture, HLHS iPSC-CMs had modest defects in sarcomere organization and calcium transient morphology compared to control. In response to cyclic stretch, control iPSC-CMs exhibited calcium transients with quicker rise time, a response observed in only one of four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that all four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs failed to upregulate calcium handling and sarcomere-associated genes in response to stretch, unlike control iPSC-CMs. Stretch also induced HLHS iPSC-CMs to exhibit pronounced activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, a response not observed in control iPSC-CMs. CONCLUSIONS: iPSC-CMs from HLHS patients demonstrate aberrant responses to cyclic stretch, including blunted adaptation of calcium transients and heightened inflammatory signaling. These findings implicate defective mechanoadaptation as a potential contributor to single ventricle failure and identify potential candidate biomarkers and new opportunities for therapeutic interventions for HLHS patients.

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) and Neurodevelopmental Disorders (NDD) frequently co-occur due to shared genetic defects in embryonic angiogenesis and mitochondrial metabolism; however, the regulatory mechanisms linking these pathways remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: To identify pathogenic genes underlying CHD-NDD co-development and investigate the regulatory role of Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Subunit C (SDHC) in endothelial angiogenesis. METHODS: Blood samples from 70 children (13 CHD+NDD, 33 CHD, 24 NDD) were analyzed by Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS). Candidate genes were identified through bidirectional deduplication, multi-library comparison, PPI network analysis, and functional enrichment analysis. SDHC expression was examined by immunofluorescence in the developing mouse heart and brain. In Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells (HUVECs) with SDHC overexpression or knockdown, eNOS and TNF-α protein levels were measured by Western blot. Cell migration and tube formation were quantified by scratch and Matrigel assays. RESULTS: WES identified high-frequency SDHC mutations, including T→TTA (Chr1:161293485, 33.33%) and C→CT (Chr1:161332091, 55.56%) in CHD+NDD. Bioinformatics suggested SDHC involvement in cardiac and neural development. In mice, cardiac SDHC increased age-dependently by 71.83% (P < 0.05), 100.21% (P < 0.01), and 239.89% (P < 0.0001) from 1 to 8 weeks. In HUVECs, SDHC overexpression upregulated eNOS by 103.25% (P < 0.001) and downregulated TNF-α by 45.16% (P < 0.01); knockdown downregulated eNOS by 43.37% (P < 0.05). SDHC overexpression increased migration by 42.96% (P < 0.0001), while its knockdown decreased it by 34.02% (P < 0.001). DISCUSSION: These findings suggest SDHC dysregulation may affect CHD-NDD comorbidity through eNOS modulation and inflammatory responses in HUVECs. However, the small cohort (n = 13 CHD + NDD), absence of healthy controls, and lack of patient-derived variant validation limit definitive conclusions. The biological consequences of the identified variants remain unknown because variant-specific functional analyses were not performed. Future studies require expanded cohorts and in vivo SDHC- specific models to investigate potential associations. These findings suggest SDHC as a candidate gene associated with CHD-NDD comorbidity.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) has become an essential imaging modality for the diagnosis and risk assessment. However, the overall knowledge structure and research trends of CMR applications in DCM remain unclear. METHOD: This study used bibliometric analysis to evaluate research on CMR in DCM from 2016 to 2025. Publications were searched from the Web of Science Core Collection database. CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used to analyze publication trends, citations, keywords, and keyword bursts. RESULTS: A total of 1,296 articles were included in this study. JACC-Cardiovascular Imaging and Circulation ranked first and second, respectively, in terms of citations. The United States, England, and Italy were the three most highly cited countries, while Harvard Medical School, Mayo Clinic, and the University of Padua were the three most highly cited institutions. The 2023 ESC Guidelines were the most highly cited reference. Based on the keyword clustering analysis, four main clusters have been identified: myocardial fibrosis, quantitative mapping, inflammatory differential diagnosis, and arrhythmia risk assessment. Burst keyword analysis revealed an evolution from conventional functional and imaging assessment toward emerging topics involving machine learning, genetics, and arrhythmic risk stratification. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that CMR research in DCM has increasingly focused on tissue characterization and imaging-based risk evaluation. Imaging markers, such as late gadolinium enhancement and parametric mapping, are gradually being applied to identify patients with a higher risk of ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death. Artificial intelligence will be used to develop a new kind of presentation for clinical data that is more accurate and user-friendly. CONCLUSION: CMR is moving beyond traditional morphological assessment and is gradually being applied in risk stratification and personalized management of DCM. Based on the knowledge structure and research development in this area, this study provides a reference for future research and the clinical translation of emerging CMR techniques.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Cardiac fibrosis is a major determinant of adverse remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), but the human disease-associated fibroblast state is incompletely resolved. We tested whether a non-classical MEOX1+FAP + ACTA2-low extracellular matrix (ECM)-remodeling state could be reproduced across independent human cardiac single-nucleus RNA-sequencing cohorts. METHODS: Public GSE183852 data (25 non-failing donor and 13 DCM hearts) were used for discovery, and SCP1303 (16 normal and 11 DCM hearts) for external validation. Fibroblasts were independently reclustered. All inferential analyses used donors as the statistical unit. State abundance was assessed with Wilcoxon tests, 10,000-iteration donor bootstrap confidence intervals, leave-one-donor-out analyses, and heteroscedasticity-robust covariate models. Raw fibroblast counts were aggregated by donor for pseudobulk differential expression with age-tertile and sex adjustment. ECM activity was compared using pseudobulk and cell-derived donor summaries. RESULTS: Discovery cluster two showed a MEOX1+FAP + ACTA2-low profile distinct from an ACTA2-high state and was enriched in DCM. Its mean abundance difference was 0.165 of fibroblasts (bootstrap 95% confidence interval 0.035-0.349), with a positive effect after omission of every donor. Age-tertile and sex adjustment preserved the effect magnitude, although the robust confidence interval marginally crossed zero. In SCP1303, the corresponding activated-fibroblast state was enriched in DCM (mean difference 0.192, bootstrap 95% confidence interval 0.144-0.256) and remained associated after sex adjustment. Donor-pseudobulk models identified higher DDAH1, MEOX1 and FAP expression in DCM after false-discovery-rate correction. Two ECM summaries were strongly correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.891), although group significance was method dependent. CONCLUSION: A reproducible MEOX1+FAP+, relatively ACTA2-low fibroblast state is associated with ECM remodeling in the analyzed human DCM cohorts. DDAH1 is a prioritized state-associated candidate, not an established causal regulator. Spatial and perturbation studies are required for mechanistic validation.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in core symptom severity and co-occurring conditions, complicating efforts to understand its genetic basis. Most genetic studies rely on binary case-control ASD definitions, which may obscure clinically meaningful variation and distinct genetic contributions across the autism spectrum. Methods: We constructed machine learning (ML)-based categorical ASD subtypes and corresponding continuous ASD subtype scores using 14 key clinical symptom measures with adjustment of sex and age among 6,355 autistic children in the Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge (SPARK) cohort by Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). We then replicated and validated these subtypes and scores among 2,717 autistic children in the Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) using a modified k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) approach. In SPARK and SSC, we further clinically validated the framework by examining associations of subtype classifications and scores with support needs, service utilization and medication use by regression models with adjustment for sex, age, genetic ancestry and socioeconomic factors. We further assessed SNP-based heritability, cell-type-specific heritability enrichment, polygenic scores (PGS) for psychiatric and cognitive traits, as well as rare copy-number variant (CNV) and de novo variant (DNV) burdens across the ML-derived ASD subtype scores adjusting for sex, age and genetic ancestry. Results: We identified three clinically distinct ASD subtypes in SPARK varying in the types of supports utilized: a high-support-needs (HSN) subtype characterized by broad developmental and functional impairments and very substantial support needs (OR = 1.63, P = 3.71 x 10 -98 ); an emotional-behavioral-support-needs (EBSN) subtype marked by severe repetitive behaviors, elevated psychiatric comorbidity; and a low-support-needs (LSN) subtype with milder symptoms and relatively lower overall support needs. The three groups were associated with differential patterns in the specific types of treatments that were most common for them, from higher intensity to lower intensity. Projected ASD subtypes and scores in SSC recapitulated the phenotypic and medication-use patterns observed in SPARK. SNP-based heritability was highest for the EBSN score (h 2 g = 0.224, SE = 0.051) followed by the HSN (h 2 g = 0.167, SE = 0.049) and LSN score (h 2 g = 0.064, SE = 0.044), with suggestive cell-type-specific heritability enrichments in fetal endodermal cells and adult motor neurons for EBSN score and fetal excitatory neurons and astrocytes for HSN score (both P < 0.05). PGS of ADHD and major depressive disorder were consistently associated with higher EBSN scores in both SPARK and SSC. Higher DNV and rare CNV burden were associated with higher HSN score in SPARK, and higher rare CNV burden was associated with higher EBSN score in SSC (P < 0.05). Conclusions: Our ML-based transferable ASD subtype framework captured clinically and genetically meaningful dimensions of ASD heterogeneity, warranting further validation in larger cohorts. Keywords: Autism spectrum disorder, phenotypic heterogeneity, subtypes, machine learning, genetic burden.
